The Cathedral's nave is covered with a coffer roof with gilding and a double-wood frame decorated with golden leaves on a beige-coloured fond, and the walls are decorated with stucco and marble. The Archbishop of Beirut sits in the heart of the choir.
3d0e6f9c-00ca-5d85-9d59-e3d8520d4abc.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
3d0e6f9c-00ca-5d85-9d59-e3d8520d4abc.history: The Saint George Cathedral is the seat of the Maronite Archdiocese in Beirut. It was built between 1884 and Palm Sunday of 1894, using stone from the Roman columns of the Temple of Deir al-Qala'a in Beit Mery. The cathedral is built on the site of an earlier church, from 1755, which was also dedicated to Saint George.

3d2f1713-cb5e-5f8f-9e65-eae62c85f39d.name: A View of Street from Istanbul
3d2f1713-cb5e-5f8f-9e65-eae62c85f39d.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
3d2f1713-cb5e-5f8f-9e65-eae62c85f39d.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; Ancient Istanbul; Abdullah Freres
3d2f1713-cb5e-5f8f-9e65-eae62c85f39d.description2: The Abdullah Frères were a group of three Ottoman brothers of Armenian descent who were world-renowned photographers. They took pictures of scenic views and notable individuals, including sultans. Most of their photography was of the Ottoman Empire. In 1867, they sold their shop in Beyazid and moved to a more favourable location in Pera.

3d414881-32eb-5cec-9499-511e26749367.name: Photograph of Bab al-Saraya
3d414881-32eb-5cec-9499-511e26749367.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
3d414881-32eb-5cec-9499-511e26749367.description2: Bab al-Saraya was the eastern gate of the city. Whilst other gates were closed at dusk, this was the only gate that was kept open until evening prayer. Thus, it was also commonly known as *bab al-masla*, meaning the worshipper's gate. The official name, Bab al-Saraya, comes from its proximity to the Serail of the Amir Fakhr al-Din by the Sursuq market. It was also located near the Amir Mansur Assaf mosque on the sea front. The gate remained intact until it was destroyed by the French authorities during the mandate era, in 1927. The headquarters of an-Nahar, a famous Lebanese newspaper, now occupy the site.

3d6a39d9-ddd3-5bbb-9a0b-ea068a2f864e.name: *The Great Mosque of Algiers*
3d6a39d9-ddd3-5bbb-9a0b-ea068a2f864e.author: Dalila Orfali
3d6a39d9-ddd3-5bbb-9a0b-ea068a2f864e.keywords: Old Algiers; traditional urban space; colonial city; Orientalism
3d6a39d9-ddd3-5bbb-9a0b-ea068a2f864e.description2: This painting was the first of Sintès' works to be bought by the museum on its opening in 1930. In actual fact it does not depict the mosque known as the "Great Mosque", but rather the "Djemâa ed-Djedid" (Jama'a al-Jadid) built in the 17th century in the style of the Turkish mosques from the city of Bursa. Here, the mosque appears overlooking the city's seafront ramparts, whilst the port neighbourhood's urban development does not appear to have begun.

3ea398ff-2713-5bdf-bb44-190566034004.name: Musée Archéologique de Sfax
3ea398ff-2713-5bdf-bb44-190566034004.author: Bechir Yazidi
3ea398ff-2713-5bdf-bb44-190566034004.history: Sfax, a port city in the east of the country, is Tunisia's economic centre and second city. Its town hall was built in the early 20th century, between 1905 and 1906. The builders and architects who oversaw its construction were largely Sicilian Italians and Tunisians. The town hall, built in an Arab architectural style, houses an archaeological museum on its ground floor which displayed mosaics and other Roman artefacts discovered in the ruins of Thyna.
3ea398ff-2713-5bdf-bb44-190566034004.description2: Located in the centre of the new town, Sfax's town hall is topped by a gored dome and overlooked by an elegant minaret with huge clocks mounted on its walls. It was built by the firm J. B. Pace under the supervision of the architect Guy. A section of the building was transformed into an archaeological museum. Today, the museum's collection covers every period of Tunisian history. It is divided between two floors and comes mostly from ancient Taparura, with contributions from the neighbouring archaeological sites at Skhira, Acholla, Tyna and some others. The collection includes many Roman mosaics, as well as ceramics, glasswork, coins and more from the Islamic era.

40e3019a-dd02-5de8-b6ab-7922650811cb.name: Grand Serail
40e3019a-dd02-5de8-b6ab-7922650811cb.description: The Grand Serail was built in the architectural style known as the "New Order" (Nizam Cedid in Ottoman Turkish), which reflected the new Ottoman military organisation. Indeed, its elevated location and austere facade are reminiscent of the Selimiye Barracks in Istanbul. The structure itself consists of two very tall floors, and a larger, 80m long facade. The eastern side consists of two symmetrical wings with two rows of 16 windows, joined in the middle by a protruding portico.
40e3019a-dd02-5de8-b6ab-7922650811cb.author: Hala Masri
40e3019a-dd02-5de8-b6ab-7922650811cb.history: The Grand Serail, or Government Palace, is used today as the Prime Minister's headquarters. It is located on a hill in downtown Beirut, close to the Lebanese Parliament. The building itself is the most important of the three Ottoman monuments on the Serail hill, and has been consistently in use for a variety of roles since its foundation in 1832.

4178a92a-1bcf-538f-a1a9-ee65fc839959.name: Saint Stephen Cathedral (Mar Estephan)
4178a92a-1bcf-538f-a1a9-ee65fc839959.description: The cathedral's construction was supervised by its architect, the Italian Giuseppe Maggiore. It overlooks the fishing port and was mainly built with local Batroun sandstone. The plan consists of a main nave, and two wards facing east and west. It has three altars, and a painting of St. Stephen lies above the central altar.
4178a92a-1bcf-538f-a1a9-ee65fc839959.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
4178a92a-1bcf-538f-a1a9-ee65fc839959.history: Saint Stephen's Cathedral (Mar Estephan) is a Maronite cathedral overlooking Batroun's harbour. It is notable for its size - being one of the biggest cathedrals in Lebanon - and its hybrid architectural style, combining a Byzanto-Roman style with Gothic influences. The cathedral was constructed in 1910 on the same site as an older church.
4178a92a-1bcf-538f-a1a9-ee65fc839959.keywords: Cathedral; St-Stephen; Byzantine; Roman; Gothic; Religion; Giosti; Giuseppe Maggiore; Batroun

41a2680e-8cf9-5ee5-a679-4297b5a1558c.name: Fındıklı
41a2680e-8cf9-5ee5-a679-4297b5a1558c.keywords: Photograph; Old İstanbul Photograph; İstanbul; Pascal Sebah
41a2680e-8cf9-5ee5-a679-4297b5a1558c.description2: Pascal Sébah (1823-1886) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. In 1857 he opened his first photography studio, *El Chark Societe Photographic*, in Istanbul and by 1873 was successful enough to open another studio in Cairo. In 1860 he moved to another studio next to the Russian Embassy in order to work with A. Laroche, who worked in Paris. He continued to work with Laroche until 1873.

423021cf-ae6a-5fd5-a257-4aa4a79ded1d.name: *Pedestal of the Obelisk in the Ancient Byzatine Hippodrome*
423021cf-ae6a-5fd5-a257-4aa4a79ded1d.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
423021cf-ae6a-5fd5-a257-4aa4a79ded1d.keywords: Istanbul photography; Byzantine and Ottoman architecture
423021cf-ae6a-5fd5-a257-4aa4a79ded1d.description2: A frequently employed device in Robertson's Istanbul photographs is the inclusion of the one or more human figures in the foreground – indeed, this is something of a trademark of Robertson’s work. There were two main reasons for the inclusion of these figures. For one thing, the artist used them as a way of creating a more natural scene. The other was to provide one or more reference points so that the photograph’s viewers could get an idea of the dimensions of the scene they were looking at and of the elements contained therein.

427783d7-27c6-57e4-9e7c-ee894a6d6e9d.name: The Hotel Excelsior at the Lido in Venice at the end of construction work
427783d7-27c6-57e4-9e7c-ee894a6d6e9d.holder: Archivio Progetti – Università Iuav di Venezia
427783d7-27c6-57e4-9e7c-ee894a6d6e9d.author: Riccardo Domenichini
427783d7-27c6-57e4-9e7c-ee894a6d6e9d.description2: The photograph shows the Hotel Excelsior on the beach of the Lido sandbar which separates the Venice lagoon from the sea. The building appears to be almost finished but not yet open: since the hotel was inaugurated in 1908, the photograph was probably shot before then. Giovanni Sardi was one of the most gifted architects of the eclectic generation. Here, he uses elements of the Moorish architecture like minarets and domes mixed with decorations in the Art Nouveau style and medieval elements, to emphasize the character of the building as a fabulous place for holidays and amusement.

4489055a-7c22-5ee2-b83a-00d5a4759ff6.name: Tripoli railway station
4489055a-7c22-5ee2-b83a-00d5a4759ff6.description: This station first opened in 1911, connecting Tripoli to the Syrian city of Homs with a single track. It later became the terminus of the famous Orient Express line, operating in the 1920s, 1930s and 1940s. The station was nationalized in 1920 during the French Mandate following its destruction by the Ottoman forces during World War I.
4489055a-7c22-5ee2-b83a-00d5a4759ff6.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
4489055a-7c22-5ee2-b83a-00d5a4759ff6.keywords: Railway; Transport; Connection; Communication; Innovation; Station; Tripoli; Lebanon

4612c67b-fdc6-5022-bc82-f418c2ebce67.name: Hotel Excelsior
4612c67b-fdc6-5022-bc82-f418c2ebce67.history: Built between 1914 and 1916, the hotel was designed by the French architect Hippolyte-Joseph Delaporte in Neo-Moorish style. It became very popular among the mainly European elite who visited the city and settled there.
4612c67b-fdc6-5022-bc82-f418c2ebce67.keywords: Moorish style; French in Morocco; French in North Africa; French architects in North Africa; protectorate; Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic influence; al-Andalus; Andalusian art; Andalusian motifs; Andalusian architecture; Islamic architecture in Morocco; Islamic art of Spain; European influence; European architecture; hotel; travel; tourism; city; urban space; changes in urban spaces; colonial city; colonial building; colonial architecture; city plan; Moroccan city; urban planning; geometrical motifs; column; capital
4612c67b-fdc6-5022-bc82-f418c2ebce67.description2: The four-storey Excelsior Hotel belongs to the style known as Neo-Moorish. The facade contains horseshoe and semi-circular windows protected by flat railings decorated with geometric motifs, some within loggias and flat and bow windows on the first floor. A balcony runs across the top floor – the roof covered in green tiles – supported by columns with capitals decorated with geometric patterns.

47ae1491-a4bf-5c5f-98f7-d10504afcb6c.name: *Hagia Sophia. General view*
47ae1491-a4bf-5c5f-98f7-d10504afcb6c.description: Photographic print that is part of an album of different Istanbul images taken by the studio of the three Armenian brothers who, in 1880, opened a headquarters in this city. It shows the central nave of the Mosque of Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya Camii), under the main dome, facing the Eastern apse where the altar has been replaced by a *mihrab*. On the left, in the transept, the pavilion for the sultan's personal prayer. A group of men are sitting on the ground, on carpets that cover the entire surface, listening attentively. This kind of album had great success with 19th century European travellers.
47ae1491-a4bf-5c5f-98f7-d10504afcb6c.author: Rebeca C. Recio

4822489f-e111-5ff5-94a1-552add25ba10.name: *St. George Church*
4822489f-e111-5ff5-94a1-552add25ba10.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
4822489f-e111-5ff5-94a1-552add25ba10.author: Stefan Weber
4822489f-e111-5ff5-94a1-552add25ba10.description2: Built by Monsignor Joseph Debs, the neo-classical cathedral was inspired by the largest Catholic Marian church in Rome, the Basilica di Santa Maria Maggiore, and bears great resemblance to it. The construction of this church, dedicated to patron saint St George, was finished in 1894. Heavily hit and looted (including an important Delacroix painting of St Georges) during the Lebanese civil war it was finally restored and re-inaugurated in April 2000.

48f017b2-30fc-5195-8291-3ffaa1a2aeb8.name: Repairing pyramids road, Cairo
48f017b2-30fc-5195-8291-3ffaa1a2aeb8.description2: The Pyramids Road was fully repaired and put into use in 1868, successfully joining Giza to Cairo. Thanks to rising tourism in the area, different modes of transport were introduced along this route: cabs and omnibuses in the 19th century, and a tramway in the 20th century. The road was finally resurfaced following the invention of the motorcar, as we can see in this photograph.

49c47898-4a5f-59d7-a4f2-c9772ec5efeb.name: Colourful Mosque
49c47898-4a5f-59d7-a4f2-c9772ec5efeb.author: Nada Andonovska
49c47898-4a5f-59d7-a4f2-c9772ec5efeb.history: This Colourful Mosque was originally built in 1438 by Isaak Bey. The construction of the mosque was financed by two sisters from Tetovo, Hurshida and Mensure. It was reconstructed in 1833 by Abdurrahman Pasha, who commissioned skilful construction masters from Debar to do the painted decoration. The octagonal *türbe* within the mosque preserves the remains of Hurshida and Mensure.
49c47898-4a5f-59d7-a4f2-c9772ec5efeb.description2: This unique mosque is distinguished by the outstanding architecture and the various painted decoration on the façades. It differs from other mosques by the motifs of landscape applied in the interior decoration, i.e., the depiction of Mecca, as well as the rare example of the illustration of the shrine of Prophet Muhammad. It does not have a distinctive exterior dome as in other mosques, but is covered by a roof in four slopes. Unlike ceramic tile decorations usually applied in traditional Ottoman mosques, the Colourful Mosque has bright paintings with floral patterns.

4a606a35-6d83-50bc-b07e-59f19aa7840a.name: Opera House, 1869
4a606a35-6d83-50bc-b07e-59f19aa7840a.notice: This is an unedited Database entry and may contain errors and inconsistencies in spelling. We are doing our best to complete the editing asap. If you are in the position to help - with a donation or as a volunteer copy-editor - please contact us at [editing@museumwnf.net](mailto:editing@museumwnf.net).

4ac252d2-71d1-5064-9680-d48fa70fd153.name: Colonial style building
4ac252d2-71d1-5064-9680-d48fa70fd153.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
4ac252d2-71d1-5064-9680-d48fa70fd153.history: In Tunis, the capital of the Protectorate imposed by France on Tunisia in 1881, the European quarter built itself right next to the old Arab medina. A new kind of home - the investment property - soon appeared, and the term balas (from the Italian palazzo) became widespread. These two or three-storey housing blocks greatly affected the city's urban landscape by introducing many different architectural styles as well as new architects, designers and builders with from different backgrounds. The 19th century was the century of eclecticism in Tunisia (both neo-classical and neo-baroque), whereas the 20th century was most marked by the influence of Art Nouveau.
4ac252d2-71d1-5064-9680-d48fa70fd153.description2:
As the name suggests, Palazzo de Guidi at 9 Rue d'Italie (now Rue Charles-de-Gaulle), was built in 1903–1906 by an Italian architect. The building has traces of different styles and influences (North African, Byzantine), and uses a variety of materials, such as stucco, mosaics, marquetery and ironwork, but as a whole it should be seen as a product of the Art Nouveau movement.  
  
The same trend of using byzantine and "oriental" motifs, but organised in a different way, is clear in the buildings at 18 and 20 Rue des Salines. Built in 1909–1910, these three-storey buildings reflect an attempt to bring together the styles of Neo-Classicism, Art Nouveau and "Arabisance", and the beautiful mosaics on the top floor with golden backgrounds are a perfect example of this.

4b63a853-7b5d-5c93-8ec7-7348d5091101.name: Model in plaster
4b63a853-7b5d-5c93-8ec7-7348d5091101.description: Following on the European fascination for the oriental world and for the famous Nasrid Palace of the Alhambra (Granada), a lot of reproductions of its remarkable architecture and decorations were made and spread. José Contreras was commended as restorer and decorator and his son, Rafael (1824–1890), was the leading pioneer of this trend in 1847. His work was continued by the grandson and by a huge number of plaster-cast workshops in Granada, and very likely, in other cities. His plasterworks were very successful in the International Exhibitions and were kept in private collections and museums like South Kensington (London). These delightful polychrome models, accentuated with a black frame, represents different rooms form the Alhambra Palace as the Comares Room, with its double horseshoe.
4b63a853-7b5d-5c93-8ec7-7348d5091101.dimensions: 68 x 41 cm; 72 x 53 and 54 x 49 cm
4b63a853-7b5d-5c93-8ec7-7348d5091101.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes, Cristina Giménez

4ba4221c-c8d6-5be1-9dda-358e2e3b0dd5.name: French plaque for Emperor Napoleon III
4ba4221c-c8d6-5be1-9dda-358e2e3b0dd5.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
4ba4221c-c8d6-5be1-9dda-358e2e3b0dd5.description2: This plaque was erected by Emperor Napoléon III during the French Beaufort d'Hautpoul campaign, a military campaign aimed at ending the conflict that broke out between the Druze and Maronite communities in 1860. The text, written in French, is composed of 14 lines and lists the names of the battalions that took part in the campaign. This plaque replaced the monument that was built here by Pharaoh Ramses II (1279-73 BC).

4bacddd8-1bf3-5cf7-ae4b-b8ebd6e26987.name: Archaeological and topographic map of the Carthaginian ruins
4bacddd8-1bf3-5cf7-ae4b-b8ebd6e26987.keywords: Phoenician, punic, roman ruins; archaeological excavations; Tunisia
4bacddd8-1bf3-5cf7-ae4b-b8ebd6e26987.description2: Having been invaded and destroyed many times, the city of Carthage was then subject to various sackings, and its ruins served as a quarry for nearby towns. The site was rediscovered in the 19th century and became fashionable following the publication of Flaubert's novel *Salammbô*. Archaeologists soon felt the need for the different sites to be mapped, and in 1833 a Danish marine, Falbe, put forward a proposal for the *Recherches sur l'Emplacement de Carthage*. Thanks to the maps drawn up by the army's geographical service and military engineers, by the end of the 19th century archaeologists were able to conduct more detailed work, particularly with regards to the division of land.

4c5ec9e7-571c-57c0-a345-64717d007c10.name: *Nazareth School*
4c5ec9e7-571c-57c0-a345-64717d007c10.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
4c5ec9e7-571c-57c0-a345-64717d007c10.description2: Pictured here is the Nazareth School, founded in 1868 by Mother Pauline de Vaux, Superior General of the Congregation of the Ladies of Nazareth. The decision to found this school was supported by the Bishop Vallegra, in Rome. It was first located in a large house in the European quarter of Beirut, nicknamed "The Blue Castle". However, with the number of students rapidly growing, the school had to relocate. In 1877 the new convent was opened for this purpose on St. George Hill, bought by the *firman* of Constantinople. The building is U-shaped and made of stone, with white cloisters and surrounded by a huge garden.

4c9b74cf-404a-5d12-81d7-a9ae783d38bb.name: Plants Museum at the Agricultural museum
4c9b74cf-404a-5d12-81d7-a9ae783d38bb.author: Ibrahim Abdel Aziz
4c9b74cf-404a-5d12-81d7-a9ae783d38bb.history:
King Fu\`ad I chose the palace of Fatma Ismail, the daughter of Khedive Ismail, ‎to host the displays of the Agricultural Museum. The ‎palace was chosen due to its location near the Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture in the ‎neighborhood of Dokki in Cairo.  
The museum, which was first called "The Agricultural Museum of King Fu\`ad I", was officially opened for the public on the 16th of January 1938 in a big ceremony that the king himself attended.
4c9b74cf-404a-5d12-81d7-a9ae783d38bb.keywords: Agricultural museum; Dokki, Agriculture Palace; Khedive Ismail; King Fu`ad I; Princess Fatma; Khedivial palaces; Khedivial Egypt; Ancient Agriculture; Pharaonic Agriculture
4c9b74cf-404a-5d12-81d7-a9ae783d38bb.description2: This building is used as a display museum to show the most important crops, cultivated plants, and food products in Egypt, as well as samples of many agricultural machines that were used in the harvesting, threshing, seed preservation and food manufacturing processes.

4d05ada4-2d34-5d8d-a4de-709d122b1851.name: *The port and pier at Algiers*
4d05ada4-2d34-5d8d-a4de-709d122b1851.archival: Berbrugger, *Algérie Historique Pittoresque et Monumentale*, Paris: J. Delahaye, 1843.

4e0c92b4-02c0-5702-a875-3dcb83eaa576.name: The Miraculous Sea Lady Church
4e0c92b4-02c0-5702-a875-3dcb83eaa576.description: This small Greek Orthodox Church overlooks the Phoenician sea wall. It is built with Batroun sandstone and using single-barrel vaulting from East to West.
4e0c92b4-02c0-5702-a875-3dcb83eaa576.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
4e0c92b4-02c0-5702-a875-3dcb83eaa576.history: Although gold icons made by Isaac of Jerusalem in 1863 were found inside this church, its construction date remains unknown.

4e167204-1a3f-5a86-944d-ab0b42f8681b.name: Parthian Monument: the adoption of the Emperors
4e167204-1a3f-5a86-944d-ab0b42f8681b.description: During his reign, the Emperor Hadrian (figure right) adopted Antoninus Pius (centre left), who in turn adopted the 17-year-old Marcus Aurelius (left) and the eight-year-old Lucius Verus. A head stares from behind Hadrian’s left shoulder, presumably representing the guardian spirit of Aelius Verus, late father of Lucius. A bull is being offered to the gods as a sacrifice.
4e167204-1a3f-5a86-944d-ab0b42f8681b.holder: Kunsthistorisches Museum, Collection of Greek and Roman Antiquities

4fba9c3c-f84d-510f-bba6-f6a6783a23b3.name: Nusretiye Mosque and the Imperial Gun Foundry in Tophane
4fba9c3c-f84d-510f-bba6-f6a6783a23b3.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
4fba9c3c-f84d-510f-bba6-f6a6783a23b3.description2: A frequently employed device in Robertson's Istanbul photographs is the inclusion of the one or more human figures in the foreground – indeed, this is something of a trademark of Robertson’s work. There were two main reasons for the inclusion of these figures. For one thing, the artist used them as a way of creating a more natural scene. The other was to provide one or more reference points so that the photograph’s viewers could get an idea of the dimensions of the scene they were looking at and of the elements contained therein.

4ff37598-ea12-5304-b2b5-a79f541ebf9d.name: Monastery of St. John at Bigor
4ff37598-ea12-5304-b2b5-a79f541ebf9d.dates: Restored in the 18th century, it was expanded and additional wings built in the span of 1812-1825
4ff37598-ea12-5304-b2b5-a79f541ebf9d.author: Nada Andonovska
4ff37598-ea12-5304-b2b5-a79f541ebf9d.history: According to monastery chronicles, the original church was built in 1020 by the first Archbishop of Ohrid, Ivan I. Debranin (1018–1037). It was ruined in the 16th century and restored by the monk Ilarion in 1743. In the span of 1812–1825 during Archimandrite Arsenie (1807–1825) major reconstruction and expansion of the monastery was carried out. From about the same time comes also the exquisite wooden iconostasis. It is considered a masterpiece of Byzantine sculptural art.
4ff37598-ea12-5304-b2b5-a79f541ebf9d.architects: Local construction masters and wood-carving craftsmen: Petre Filipovski Garkata, his brother Marko Filipovski and Makarija Frchkovski
4ff37598-ea12-5304-b2b5-a79f541ebf9d.description2: Situated on the steep slopes of the Bistra Mountain near Debar and rising above the banks of the Radika river, the Monastery of St. John at Bigor is one of the most beautiful edifices in Macedonia. The church within the Monastery is devoted to St. John the Baptist. It preserves the exquisitely carved walnut iconostasis. The iconostasis, which depicts scenes from the Old and the New Testaments, was created by the most outstanding Macedonian masters of wood-carving: Petre Filipovski Garkata and his brothers Marko and Makarij Frchkovski. The monastery complex nowadays comprises the monastery church, the chamber-tomb, defence tower, icon gallery arranged in the dining room and the monastery lodgings.

509dc50d-cdf0-5d63-8c8f-6dcddd22c1f2.name: Bullfight Arena of Campo Pequeno
509dc50d-cdf0-5d63-8c8f-6dcddd22c1f2.author: Cristina Correia
509dc50d-cdf0-5d63-8c8f-6dcddd22c1f2.history:
In 1821 King João VI hands over the organization of non free bullfights to Real Casa Pia de Lisboa, an educational institution founded by his mother in 1780 to support youngsters in risk. To overcome the exiguity of its first arena, in 1889 Casa Pia orders a new one to architect António Dias da Silva who sent the plans from Madrid according to the meanwhile disappeared Neo-Mudejar Bullfight Arena of Madrid by Emilio Rodriguez Ayuso. Built between 1890-1892 it will be inaugurated still unfinished by Royal Prince Afonso of Braganza (1865–1920) on the 18th August 1892.  
From those days onwards keeps being one of the main bullfight arenas in Portugal nowadays renovated and transformed into a multifunctional venue.
509dc50d-cdf0-5d63-8c8f-6dcddd22c1f2.keywords: Architecture; Arab Style; Leisure; Bullfight arena; Lisbon
509dc50d-cdf0-5d63-8c8f-6dcddd22c1f2.third_name: Campo de Touros do Campo Pequeno
509dc50d-cdf0-5d63-8c8f-6dcddd22c1f2.description2: The Bullfight arena, built with monochromatic brick, is an iconic example of the 19th century neo-Arab style in Lisbon, was the neo-Mudejar one in Madrid. With an external perimeter of 80 m, its circular plan includes 4 polygonal towers attached symmetrically and topped by bulbous domes originally polychromatic. The 40.7 m diameter arena was covered with sand, encircled by a wooden fence and separated from the circular rows of seats by a corridor. It seats 8,438 spectators three levels namely in five rows mounted on an iron structure and two rows of 165 lodges and galleries. The access is provided by two 3 m wide covered walks. One of its main features is the use of the brick particularly enhanced on the segments of the several arches rhythmically opened at the external walls.

50c481c2-3b97-5936-ae28-31d363a507e2.name: Traditional Lebanese house
50c481c2-3b97-5936-ae28-31d363a507e2.description: Traditional Lebanese houses in the 19th century were generally rather modest. The roofs were supported by wooden beams, and were accessible by an internal stairway made of stone, compared to the wooden stairways of more modest abodes.
50c481c2-3b97-5936-ae28-31d363a507e2.history: The houses were built with wooden windows which were filled with tinted glass. A balcony could usually be found on the first floor, which was covered with a clear window for lighting and ventilation purposes. This architectural style was clearly influenced by European architecture and design, indicating the growing influence of European culture and trends in 19th century Beirut and elsewhere in the region.

51101afe-20b5-5b27-9fe9-38dbf49761d6.name: The Imam Uza'i Mosque
51101afe-20b5-5b27-9fe9-38dbf49761d6.author: Hala Masri
51101afe-20b5-5b27-9fe9-38dbf49761d6.history: The name of Imam Uza'i, who died twelve centuries ago, is often associated with the values of tolerance, justice, and brotherhood. Born in Baalbek in the year 681, 'Abd al-Rahman Uza'i was a strong advocate of justice, freedom and mercy over what he considered to be the religious fanaticism and human autocracy of his time. He stood alongside Lebanese Christians in his fervent opposition to the Abbasid regime. He was also a renowned thinker and intellectual. After relocating to Beirut he soon begun to accept visitors in his home where he offered advice and imparted wisdom. To this day, thousands of Lebanese visit his mausoleum in search for blessings and mercy.
51101afe-20b5-5b27-9fe9-38dbf49761d6.description2: The Imam Uza'i Mosque, with its green dome and two minarets, contains the tomb of Imam Uza'i, who died in 774. It became a religious school in the 19th century which is still in use today.

5213376b-6aff-55de-afcc-32cf7bfb66d1.name: Portrait of Paul Draneht
5213376b-6aff-55de-afcc-32cf7bfb66d1.author: Massimiliano Cremona, Ignazio Galella
5213376b-6aff-55de-afcc-32cf7bfb66d1.second_name: Paul Draneht (1815–1894), the Superintendent of the Cairo Opera who commissioned Aida from Giuseppe Verdi
5213376b-6aff-55de-afcc-32cf7bfb66d1.description2:
Paul Draneht (1815-1894) was born in Nicosia (Cyprus) as Pavlos Pavlidis. He was the child of a Greek Christian Orthodox family who fled Cyprus due to the clashes between Greeks and Turks, and took refuge in Egypt. Muhammad (Mehmet) Ali Pasha (the Khedive of Egypt) sent him to study in France. Trusted by the Khedive (who awarded him the titles of Bey and Pasha), Paul Draneht participated in the negotiations regarding the opening of the Suez Canal.  
He became superintendent of the Egyptian Opera Theatre and commissioned the opera Aida to the Italian composer Giuseppe Verdi. The Aida opened in Cairo on 24 December 1871.

52eaca9c-9b61-57ba-8d7c-426a9c33c3f1.name: Lithographs after the panoramic photograph taken by Robertson and Beato, *Faust: Poligrafisch Illustrirte*, Zeitschrift, 1857, Vienna
52eaca9c-9b61-57ba-8d7c-426a9c33c3f1.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
52eaca9c-9b61-57ba-8d7c-426a9c33c3f1.keywords: Istanbul panorama; Faust; tower of War Ministry in Beyazıt
52eaca9c-9b61-57ba-8d7c-426a9c33c3f1.description2: James Robertson is the first Istanbul photographer known to have taken 360 degree panoramic photographs of the city. The first panorama, which was taken in May 1854 from the War Ministry tower in Beyazıt, consists of twelve separate photographs. The most successful printed reproductions based on Robertson’s photographs curiously enough were produced in Vienna. Issues of *Faust* published during 1857 report fascinating bits of information as well as pictures that are important to the history of printing and visual arts in the Ottoman Empire. A plate published in *Faust* contained a panoramic view from the Istanbul Beyazıt tower that is made from Robertson’s panorama.

54c83199-c653-5912-a4b8-adeaddd7f3e5.name: Sursuq Palace
54c83199-c653-5912-a4b8-adeaddd7f3e5.description: Built in 1860 for Musa Sursuq, in Rue Sursuq, Sursuq Palace is now the residence of his grand-daughter Lady Yvonne Cochrane, who inherited the estate at the age of two. Of all the Sursuq houses, this is the largest and the only one that preserves its original splendour. Its second owner, Lady Cochrane's father Alfred Bey Sursuq, increased the size of the gardens and expanded the house's collection of valuable pictures, carpets and objets d'art.
54c83199-c653-5912-a4b8-adeaddd7f3e5.author: Jeff El-Msanne
54c83199-c653-5912-a4b8-adeaddd7f3e5.history: Other than some nineteenth century plaster-work in the reception rooms which resembles Sicilian palaces of the time, and the employment of some Italian craftsmen, the Sursuq House was built in a strictly traditional Lebanese architectural and aesthetic style. This is indicated first and foremost by the use of a single large block. The Great Hall consists of four sets of traditional Lebanese triple-arches, each supported by fluted marble pillars. The house’s painted furnishings were commissioned and designed privately. It also contains a series of glass cabinets, displaying various valuable collections, including second century glassware and Lebanese jewellery. The garden is one of the largest gardens left in the city, with many landowners having sold their properties to speculative building projects. The kiosk in the garden, which was converted into a Turkish baths when the house was built in 1860, predates the main house and is used as visitor rooms today.

559330fc-4f61-535a-9310-1782a48a785a.name: The Tell Clock Tower
559330fc-4f61-535a-9310-1782a48a785a.description: This clock tower is located in Al-Tell square, next to Al-Manshiyya, one of the oldest parks in Tripoli. The tower is 30 metres tall and consists of five separate floors.
559330fc-4f61-535a-9310-1782a48a785a.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
559330fc-4f61-535a-9310-1782a48a785a.history: This clock tower was gifted to the city of Tripoli - like many clock towers of the Ottoman Empire, such as the famous Jaffa clock tower - and erected in 1906, to celebrate the 30th anniversary of Sultan 'Abd al-Hamid II's reign. The clock tower is now working again, following a full renovation in 1992, supported by personal funding from the honorary Turkish consul of Northern Lebanon, Sobhi Akkari.

574d6f3c-2cbb-5d5b-9f00-e0dd275b71a9.name: *Excavation of the Great Temple of Ramesses II at Abu Simbel*
574d6f3c-2cbb-5d5b-9f00-e0dd275b71a9.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
574d6f3c-2cbb-5d5b-9f00-e0dd275b71a9.description2:
An intrepid and versatile Frenchman, Linant came to Egypt in 1818. In Cairo he adopted the life of an Ottoman Turk, but was known and consulted by European residents and visitors as well as by the Pasha of Egypt, Muhammad Ali. At various times his talents were employed as a geographer, explorer, engineer, cartographer and draughtsman.  
His first adventure was an expedition to Upper Egypt that Henry Salt, British Consul-General in Egypt , took to Abu Simbel in 1818-19. Although there were other artists in the party it is likely that this watercolour is by Linant and that it depicts Salt's attempts to clear away the ever encroaching sand from the facade of the Great Temple. Linant took part in several subsequent expeditions up the Nile, and was one of the first Europeans to reach the Pharaonic sites of Meroe and Musawarat.

58b9f9f7-6b17-532d-8f51-0f4b19d4fb8d.name: *Vue d'Alger*
58b9f9f7-6b17-532d-8f51-0f4b19d4fb8d.author: Dalila Orfali
58b9f9f7-6b17-532d-8f51-0f4b19d4fb8d.description2: These two original lithographs depict the city of al-Jaza'ir (Algiers) prior to the English bombardment led by Lord Exmouth on 26 August 1816. The regency was ruled first by the *Beylerbeys* (general governors) from 1518 to 1587, then by the Pashas from 1587 to 1659, the *Aghas* from 1659 to 1671 and the Deys from 1671 to 1830. The reign of the final Dey of Algiers, Hussein, lasted 12 years until the French conquest in 1830.

59043927-aae8-5c23-9db7-2ff253833d51.name: *The political refugee*
59043927-aae8-5c23-9db7-2ff253833d51.second_name: Illustration for "The Bohemians of Paris", *Le Charivari* 11
59043927-aae8-5c23-9db7-2ff253833d51.description2: The cartoonist Honoré Daumier (1808–1879) was one of the first to be interested in the theme of migration, and drew many cartoon strips which dealt with the difficulties of exile. He did some more comic drawings on this theme, which are harder to understand. In this image, published in a series on the theme of the "Bohemian" (an artistic community attempting to live without restrictions), he highlights the gaze of his contemporaries on the "other" or the "stranger". The image also mocks the suspicious young woman just as much as the asylum seeker.

59764ffc-10d9-5e4d-8967-5888b3e97194.name: National Museum of Soares dos Reis
59764ffc-10d9-5e4d-8967-5888b3e97194.history: The Carrancas Palace is a neo-classical palace built by the Moraes e Castro family, which accommodated the English generals during the Napoleonic Invasions, and was later converted into a royal residence. The National Museum of Soares dos Reis, established by King Pedro IV in 1833, was Portugal’s first public museum and was inspired by the cultural and heritage protecting spirit typical of Liberalism.
59764ffc-10d9-5e4d-8967-5888b3e97194.keywords: Neoclassicism; Oporto; Palace; Museum; History of Art
59764ffc-10d9-5e4d-8967-5888b3e97194.description2:
The Carrancas Palace is an imposing neoclassical building with four main areas: the U-shaped noble area, the galleries, the closed central courtyard and the backyard. Despite having been converted into a museum, the palace has preserved most of its original structure.  
The building interior has a refined decoration, shown in the stuccoes embellishing the dining room and the furniture in the music room, both of which were inspired on the creations of Robert Adams.

5a77c00d-9eb8-5458-82b1-be2e4374f487.name: The House of Shaykh Said bin Mohammed al-Qasimi
5a77c00d-9eb8-5458-82b1-be2e4374f487.holder: Sharjah Museums Authority / Sharjah Heritage Directorate
5a77c00d-9eb8-5458-82b1-be2e4374f487.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
5a77c00d-9eb8-5458-82b1-be2e4374f487.notice: Please note that this is an unedited database entry and that it may contain grammatical errors and inconsistencies in spelling. We are working to raise the funds required to complete the editing of the database; should you wish to contribute please visit our [Support page](https://www.museumwnf.org/atrium_support.php).
5a77c00d-9eb8-5458-82b1-be2e4374f487.third_name: Bayt al-Shaykh Said bin Mohammed al-Qasimi
5a77c00d-9eb8-5458-82b1-be2e4374f487.description2: Bayt al-Shaykh Said bin Mohammed al-Qasimi (today comprehensively restored) was built between 1898 and 1901 for the local Qasimi ruler. A single-storeyed house with windowless surrounding walls, it follows the traditional layout of a local residence arranged around a central courtyard. Its majlis or reception room is unusually large, with a tall central column and beam construction enabling the space to be considerably widened beyond the more commonly applied dimensions. Bait al Shaikh Said bin Mohammed Al Qasimi witnessed the signing of several trucial agreements with the British pertinent to the whole region.

5aae14de-96b5-54d8-bde0-643bb24e8c93.name: Palace of Mulay ʿAbd al-Hafiz
5aae14de-96b5-54d8-bde0-643bb24e8c93.history: Built in the era of Mulay Isma‘il (mid-18th century) by the architect-Pasha ‘Ali al-Rifi, the palace was renovated and adapted by Mulay al-Hasan I’s son, ‘Abd al-Hafiz. However, the latter never lived there because he was exiled to Spain by the French before it was completed, but as a condition of signing the Deed of Protectorate, ‘Abd al-Hafiz insisted that the works be completed. When the restoration was completed in 1912 the palace was ceded to France and sold at auction. In 1926, the palace and the surrounding park were acquired by the Italian government, which turned it into a school, hospital and church. Known also as the Palace of Italian Institutions, it was used as a venue for receptions, exhibitions, and music and theatre performances. Abandoned after independence, the building has recently been restored.
5aae14de-96b5-54d8-bde0-643bb24e8c93.keywords: Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic architecture in Morocco; Islamic influence; Moroccan architects; traditional city; Islamic city; palace; royal palace; garden; Islamic garden; gardens and architecture; plan; urban planning; Moorish style; patio; portico; column; al-Andalus; Andalusian architecture; Andalusian influence; European architecture; European influence; artistic exchanges; column; capital; classicism; Italian influence; Italian marble; protectorate
5aae14de-96b5-54d8-bde0-643bb24e8c93.description2: Renovated and adapted in the late 19th century by Sultan Mulay ‘Abd al-Hafiz, the palace is a masterpiece of Neo-Moorish style architecture, which can be seen in the beauty of its gardens, facade and interiors. Located in the central district of Hasnouna, the estate covers an area of 32,800m2, of which 8,669m2 are occupied by the palace building, which is organised around a large portico-covered courtyard with a central fountain. The Moorish or Arab-Andalusian style of the palace has accents from the European architectural vocabulary, seen for example in the Italianesque marble Neo-Corinthian column capitals decorated with crescent moons.

5aee46c9-4c7b-55fb-bca1-375579387666.name: Barbadinhos steam pumping station at the time of its inauguration
5aee46c9-4c7b-55fb-bca1-375579387666.holder: Historical Archive, Empresa Portuguesa das Águas Livres (Portuguese Water Company)
5aee46c9-4c7b-55fb-bca1-375579387666.dimensions: Rectangular shape; length: 26 cm, width: 18 cm. Mounted on cardboard (30,5 x 24,5 cm)
5aee46c9-4c7b-55fb-bca1-375579387666.author: AHEPAL–EPAL’s Historical Archive
5aee46c9-4c7b-55fb-bca1-375579387666.keywords: Lisbon; water supply; Innovation; Industrial Archeology
5aee46c9-4c7b-55fb-bca1-375579387666.second_name: Central Pumping Station of Barbadinhos, machines storehouse, main or south façade
5aee46c9-4c7b-55fb-bca1-375579387666.description2: This picture is part of an album entitled "Canal Alviela / Inauguration / 3 October 1880" that includes 10 photographs by Francesco Rocchini. The picture depicts the main façade of the Barbadinhos steam pumping station at the time of its inauguration. The chimney and the engine room of the water reservoir of Barbadinhos can be seen on the right side of the picture. The steam station was in operation until 1928, when a new electrically powered station was opened. After decommissioning, the machines were not dismantled and are currently preserved. The building of the Barbadinhos steam pumping station houses the Water Museum (opened in 1987) and was classified in 2010 as a building of public interest.

5ce76956-57f6-57ef-9da7-fc2a688258ea.name: Beylerbeyi Palace
5ce76956-57f6-57ef-9da7-fc2a688258ea.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
5ce76956-57f6-57ef-9da7-fc2a688258ea.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; Ancient Istanbul; palace
5ce76956-57f6-57ef-9da7-fc2a688258ea.description2: Beylerbeyi Palace was commissioned by Sultan Abdülaziz (1830-76) and built between 1861 and 1865 as a summer residence and a place to entertain visiting heads of state. The Palace was designed by Sarkis Balyan in the second Empire. It looks its most attractive from the Bosporus, from which its two bathing pavilions – one for the *harem* (women's only) and the other for the *selamlik* (men's only) – can best be seen. One of the most attractive rooms is the reception hall, which has a pool and fountain. Running water was popular in Ottoman houses for its pleasant sound and cooling effect in the heat.

5dc4fbc5-e8e9-52ae-aa62-690ee8359b41.name: Lake d'Orta. Villa Crespi
5dc4fbc5-e8e9-52ae-aa62-690ee8359b41.author: Ignazio Galella
5dc4fbc5-e8e9-52ae-aa62-690ee8359b41.description2:
Cristoforo Benigno Crespi was a successful businessman active in the cotton industry. In 1879, he bought an estate near the lake d’Orta (Piedmont, Northern Italy), in order to build a vacation house in honour of his wife, Pia Travelli.  
He had fallen in love with the architecture of Baghdad, where he went to buy cotton, and asked architect Angelo Colla to build a villa in the Moorish style. Architect Enrico Combi designed the magnificent park.  
The villa features a 48-meter high minaret and has richly decorated interiors, made with marbles of great value, imported from several different countries. It required 12 year of works to be completed. The estate comprises a greenhouse, a wet dock, stables, a big fountain, an annex, and is surrounded by walls, with valuable wrought iron gates.

601e5d3a-e68f-587a-846c-d0f3657cf4f6.name: *Dar al-Baladiyya, Damascus*
601e5d3a-e68f-587a-846c-d0f3657cf4f6.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
601e5d3a-e68f-587a-846c-d0f3657cf4f6.author: Stefan Weber
601e5d3a-e68f-587a-846c-d0f3657cf4f6.second_name: City Hall at the new urban centre at Merje Square
601e5d3a-e68f-587a-846c-d0f3657cf4f6.description2: Built between 1892 to 1894, the Dar al-Baladiyya was a prestigious edifice in stone. With its neo-classical elements and prominent middle projection, it was designed to display the power of the “new” state. The purpose of building the City Hall was functional, since the administrative workload, which rapidly increased after the reforms of the administrative system had to be accommodated.

604ea0d6-64f6-5863-9076-425493fdad68.name: Lincoln Hotel
604ea0d6-64f6-5863-9076-425493fdad68.description: The Lincoln Hotel, constructed out of load-bearing masonry, has three floors supported by steel beams with brick vaults, plus the ground floor and a small terrace located in the middle. Its Neo-Moorish style is notable for having several features: a red-tiled roof; pointed horseshoe arches on the first and second-floor windows; and corbelled arches, which accentuate the porch that opens up across the lower part of this grand building. The front facade is enriched with columns, which are topped with capitals decorated with floral ornamentation. The Lincoln was the first hotel to be built in the city, in an area devoted to the accommodation and entertainment of European visitors and settlers.
604ea0d6-64f6-5863-9076-425493fdad68.history: The Lincoln Hotel was designed in the Neo-Moorish style by the French architect Hubert Bride. It is an elegant mix of Arab‒Andalusian architecture with some elements introduced from the recently acquired European architectural vocabulary.
604ea0d6-64f6-5863-9076-425493fdad68.keywords: Moorish style; French in Morocco; French in North Africa; French architects in North Africa; protectorate; Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic influence; al-Andalus; Andalusian art; Andalusian motifs; Andalusian architecture; Islamic architecture in Morocco; Islamic art of Spain; European influence; European architecture; hotel; travel; tourism; city; urban space; changes in urban spaces; colonial city; Moroccan city; colonial building; colonial architecture; plan; urban planning

60bbc9e6-fb95-527b-9468-c85f9f19bc5b.name: Map of Oran
60bbc9e6-fb95-527b-9468-c85f9f19bc5b.archival: Ravoisié, A., *Exploration scientifique de l'Algérie pendant les annéees 1840-1841-1842*, vol. I, Paris: 1846.

6129ee64-d66a-53c2-9b9c-8ac38a87b8b9.name: Moroccan House in Linderhof  Palace Park
6129ee64-d66a-53c2-9b9c-8ac38a87b8b9.type: Pavillion; Park building in Linderhof Palace Park
6129ee64-d66a-53c2-9b9c-8ac38a87b8b9.history:
When the rebuilding of the “Moorish Kiosk” in the Linderhof park undertaken by order of Ludwig II was completed at the beginning of 1878, it evidently reawakened the king’s interest in buildings in the Islamic architectural style.  
The pavilion, acquired at the World Exhibition in Paris in 1878, was remodelled inside at Ludwig II's request and originally built on the Stockalpe near the Austrian border. The "Moroccan House" had already also been shown at the International Exhibition in Vienna in 1873 and had been built for this purpose in Morocco. The wooden building, acquired by a private individual after the king's death, was bought back by the state in 1980 and was reconstructed in the palace park in 1998.
6129ee64-d66a-53c2-9b9c-8ac38a87b8b9.keywords: King Ludwig II; Linderhof Palace; Ettal; Moorish style; Romanticism; gardens
6129ee64-d66a-53c2-9b9c-8ac38a87b8b9.description2: The king had considerable alterations made to both the outside and the inside of the house in keeping with his own lavish tastes. Jean Perron, a sculptor in Paris who had organised the purchase for Ludwig II, also acquired the rich furnishings appropriate for an ornamental setting such as tables, chandeliers, tabourets, mirrors and vessels, none of which have been preserved. Numerous skilled workers and artists were involved in the dismantling, rebuilding and altering of the house.The entire colour scheme was changed with an abundant use of gold, and individual rooms were furnished with costly materials. Coloured glazing “in the Moorish style” and a tessellated floor were introduced to add to the oriental character of the house.

61dba05c-1c18-5736-85f3-727803bfc389.name: *Housing in the Pierrefitte Chateau and Gardens* \[…\] *Payable in installments* \[…\] *\[Epargne Foncière Immobilière des Quinze - Vingts\]: open to visitors every day.*
61dba05c-1c18-5736-85f3-727803bfc389.description2: Pierrefitte-sur-Seine was still a farming village in the mid 19th century. The construction of the Paris-Lille railway line in 1859 brought in rich Parisians in search of country air. The town was transformed again in the 20th century, thanks to the construction of factories in the Saint-Demis plains and the arrival of people looking for cheaper housing. The first tramway was also built in 1901. This poster advertises housing in an area outside the tramway's reach, which had remained wooded and rural, and was equipped with the most modern technologies available, such as gas and telephone.

635f5f5e-120a-51d8-b033-3d0504a831cb.name: Rumelihisarı İskelesi
635f5f5e-120a-51d8-b033-3d0504a831cb.keywords: Photograph; Old İstanbul Photograph; İstanbul; Abdullah Brothers
635f5f5e-120a-51d8-b033-3d0504a831cb.description2: Abdullah Brothers is the name given to three men with Armenian origin, Viçen (1820-1902), Hovsep Abdullahyan (1830-1908) and Kevork (1839-1918) who started the art of photography in Turkey. For 40 years they photographed the people of Istanbul, landscapes, various political and social events, and prepared albums of historical and cultural values, as well as monuments.

640180dd-059b-54fe-a33c-0700c3dd70f8.name: Photograph of the Beirut–Aleppo railway
640180dd-059b-54fe-a33c-0700c3dd70f8.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
640180dd-059b-54fe-a33c-0700c3dd70f8.keywords: Transport; Railway; Communication; Connection; Innovation; Aleppo; Lebanon
640180dd-059b-54fe-a33c-0700c3dd70f8.description2: The second railway built in Lebanon opened in 1906 and ran from Beirut to Aleppo in present-day Syria. It connected with the first railway line at Riyaq. The connection between Aleppo and Beirut, a well-equipped and sizeable port, decreased trade in Alexandretta, the traditional port for merchandise leaving or entering Syria. Alexandretta was not connected to Aleppo by rail until 1914. Aleppo and Northern Syria became increasingly important as links between Damascus and Beirut were consolidated. This also marked the increasing importance of Beirut as a powerful city in the region and not only as a Mediterranean port.

640cbdc1-fd31-5fad-89d3-4deff3b9943f.name: Municipal theatre
640cbdc1-fd31-5fad-89d3-4deff3b9943f.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
640cbdc1-fd31-5fad-89d3-4deff3b9943f.history: This building, which was once the Municipal Casino and often affectionately known as the "bonbonnière Resplandy", was built in the early 20th century in the Art Nouveau style by the French Architect Jean-Émile Resplandy and located on Avenue Jules-Ferry (now Avenue Habib-Bourguiba) in the heart of the European quarter. It has been constantly active since its birth, clearing the way for new artistic talent. The biggest names in Tunisian and Arab performing arts stood on its stage, performing ballet, opera, dramatic performances, classical concerts and more. In 2011 it became an important symbol of the Tunisian revolution; protestors, martyrs and rebels from all sides stood on its steps at some point.
640cbdc1-fd31-5fad-89d3-4deff3b9943f.keywords: Art Nouveau; theatre; stucco; bas reliefs; Apollo
640cbdc1-fd31-5fad-89d3-4deff3b9943f.description2: This theatre, the last remnant of a municipal artistic complex, can hold up to 1,350 seats. An immense white building, it reflects the style of Art Nouveau with evidence for some baroque influences. The bas-relief decorations, showing a scene with Apollo and the two muses, dominate the façade. The interior, from the vestibule to foyer, is notable for its modern structure and the richness of the carved stucco decorations. The bas-reliefs, moulds, cornices and balconies were all made by famous French and Italian artists.

67353cca-0fe5-559e-ad36-0dee24d15bc8.name: Dar al-Maqri
67353cca-0fe5-559e-ad36-0dee24d15bc8.holder: OFPPT / Office de la formation professionnelle et de la promotion du travail
67353cca-0fe5-559e-ad36-0dee24d15bc8.history: The gardens or *riyadh* are the work of Idris al-Muqri, the brother of the grand vizier Hajj Muhammad, and head of the *muhtasib*, the supervising authority that oversaw the quality of production. Located in the neighbourhood of Oued Sowafine (river), it was built in the early 20th century.
67353cca-0fe5-559e-ad36-0dee24d15bc8.keywords: Palace; house; Moroccan house; traditional house; Islamic house; Islamic city; Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic influence; North African house; private space; Moroccan city; Moroccan architects; Islamic architecture in Morocco; garden; Islamic garden; gardens and architecture
67353cca-0fe5-559e-ad36-0dee24d15bc8.description2: Located in an irregular and rugged area, the site consists of several pavilions and interconnected buildings, with many corridors and passages, each of which is organised around a terrace. The rooms are large, distinguished by their carved and painted domes and wall-fountains, which are tiled, and have carved, stone basins. The garden of around 2,000m2 is preceded by a *menza* or terrace, covered with tiles, and decorated with a central fountain. It offers panoramic views of the *Medina*.

6865c8bb-97f7-50ee-addb-18169728d2a9.name: *View Looking across the Hall of Columns, Karnak*
6865c8bb-97f7-50ee-addb-18169728d2a9.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
6865c8bb-97f7-50ee-addb-18169728d2a9.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
6865c8bb-97f7-50ee-addb-18169728d2a9.description2: Roberts' viewpoint across the Great Hypostyle Hall, in the Precinct of Amon-Re, at the Temple Complex at Karnak, captures in great detail the physical features of the monument as it appeared in his day. At the same time, he used exaggerated proportions to convey the structure’s imposing scale, which impressed him deeply. In his diary he writes: ’Karnak is even more astonishing than Luxor. Its magnificence is unimaginable. Trying to describe rationally what I have seen would be ridiculous’. In the 19th century,, the Karnak temple complex became one of the most famous ancient Egyptian sites visted by artists and archaeologists. During his travels up and down the Nile, Roberts captured over 300 monuments and ruins in his unprecedentedly detailed and precise works, many of them before excavation or restoration.  In his work, Roberts also drew on the pioneering scholarship of scholars like Champollion. The final depictions subtlely contributed to the Orientalist discourse on Ancient Egypt, which Europe increasingly saw as their right to appropriate.
6865c8bb-97f7-50ee-addb-18169728d2a9.artist_birthplace: David Roberts: Edinburgh, Scotland; Louis Hague: Tournai, Belgium
6865c8bb-97f7-50ee-addb-18169728d2a9.artist_deathplace: David Roberts: London; Louis Hague: London

69063980-1b98-599a-87aa-a06e11b7637c.name: Colonial style building
69063980-1b98-599a-87aa-a06e11b7637c.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
69063980-1b98-599a-87aa-a06e11b7637c.history: In Tunis, the capital of the Protectorate imposed by France on Tunisia in 1881, the European quarter built itself right next to the old Arab medina. A new kind of home - the investment property - soon appeared, and the term balas (from the Italian *palazzo*) became widespread. These two or three-storey housing blocks greatly affected the city's urban landscape by introducing many different architectural styles as well as new architects, designers and builders with from different backgrounds. The 19th century was the century of eclecticism in Tunisia (both neo-classical and neo-baroque), whereas the 20th century was most marked by the influence of Art Nouveau.
69063980-1b98-599a-87aa-a06e11b7637c.description2:
These two residential buildings at 40 and 42 Rue Oum-Kalthoum are two remarkable examples of the Art Nouveau architecture, built between 1906 and 1908. The façades are decorated with a beautiful pattern of cherubs, ribbons, small female heads and garlands, all organised with symmetrically.  
  
The Azerm Building at 53 Avenue de Carthage, built between 1905 and 1906, is a private residence. It is notable for its curved lines, balconies with irregular arches and walled niches. The abundance of rich decorations are evidence of the craftsmen's excellent skill. These buildings are perfect examples of the rich decorations of neo-baroque architecture, the huge curls of Art Nouveau, and the abundance of rococo architecture.

6acad3a4-63f3-5160-bf8e-60081e141ee0.name: Street map of Beirut
6acad3a4-63f3-5160-bf8e-60081e141ee0.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Julien El Khoury
6acad3a4-63f3-5160-bf8e-60081e141ee0.keywords: Commerce; Map; Streets; Shops; Railway; Maritime
6acad3a4-63f3-5160-bf8e-60081e141ee0.description2: This map of Beirut was drawn in in 1902 under the reign of Sultan 'Abd al-Hamid II. The table on the left contains a numbered list of shops and important landmarks, whereas the table on the right lists the name and location of Beirut's railway and maritime companies.

6b3e84b4-acb3-5d73-a5b0-e7455c527cf6.name: Map of the different types of housing in East Beirut
6b3e84b4-acb3-5d73-a5b0-e7455c527cf6.holder: *Maisons traditionnelles de Beyrouth: Typologie, culture domestique, valeur patrimoniale. Le secteur de Rmeil-Médawwar* (Book)
6b3e84b4-acb3-5d73-a5b0-e7455c527cf6.author: Jeff El-Msanne, David Andos
6b3e84b4-acb3-5d73-a5b0-e7455c527cf6.description2: This map indicates the different types of housing found in the East Beirut with a system of coloured dots.

6c348586-1356-5ba4-b2b5-0c09d19282dc.name: The Victims of Labour
6c348586-1356-5ba4-b2b5-0c09d19282dc.author: Marina Minozzi
6c348586-1356-5ba4-b2b5-0c09d19282dc.keywords: Sculpture; Italian sculptors; realism; Verismo; social topics; post-unitarian Italian society; rights of workers; working class; life expectancy; poverty; industry; communication; industrial development; road; railway; international; universal exposition
6c348586-1356-5ba4-b2b5-0c09d19282dc.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
6c348586-1356-5ba4-b2b5-0c09d19282dc.description2: Vincenzo Vela studied at the academy of Fine arts of Brera and at the age of 22 he won an Academy of Venice competition. The artwork is an homage to the workers who died during the construction of the Gotthard Tunnel between 1872-82, which had implemented new cost-lowering techniques that also caused numerous incidents and loss of life. Work conditions were very unhealthy: temperatures over 30 degrees, gas exhalations and no air shafts. Even the accommodations were unhealthy and dirty. When the workers went on strike for the inhumane conditions, police shot at protesters, killing four workers. The miners in *The Victims of Labour* are depicted carrying the body of a dying classmate on a stretcher out of the tunnel. A self-portrait of the sculptor is recognisable in the classmate’s face. The harsh modelling of the workers’ bodies, almost deformed, makes the scene even more powerful. The artist affirmed he had no commission for this work which was a passion project. In 1895 it was cast in bronze on request of the Ministry of Education; in 1900 it was sent to the Universal Exhibition in Paris.
6c348586-1356-5ba4-b2b5-0c09d19282dc.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

en: Zanchetti, G., in Elena di Majo and Mateo Lafranconi (eds), *Galleria Nazionale d’Arte Moderna. Le Collezioni. Il XIX secolo*, Milan: Electa, 2006, cat. F.4.

6c5fc9c1-bb88-513e-a896-4dd682e2510a.name: Pera Palace Hotel
6c5fc9c1-bb88-513e-a896-4dd682e2510a.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
6c5fc9c1-bb88-513e-a896-4dd682e2510a.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; Ancient Istanbul; hotel; travelling
6c5fc9c1-bb88-513e-a896-4dd682e2510a.description2: Pera Palace Hotel was built in 1892 for the purpose of hosting the passengers of the Orient Express and was named after its location. Alexander Vallaury, a French-Turkish architect living in the city designed the hotel in a blend of neo-classical, art nouveau and oriental styles. The hotel was the first building in Turkey to be powered by electricity other than the Ottoman Palaces. It was also the only address in the city to provide hot running water for its guests and was home to the first electric elevator in Istanbul.

6ce39e0b-ba14-5c06-b2e2-792e36cfa958.name: House
6ce39e0b-ba14-5c06-b2e2-792e36cfa958.dates: End of 19th – beginning of the 20th century
6ce39e0b-ba14-5c06-b2e2-792e36cfa958.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Prof. Petar Namichev (consultant)
6ce39e0b-ba14-5c06-b2e2-792e36cfa958.history: The most active period of construction by the *tajfas* from this area was in the 19th century and the beginning of the 20th century. Construction masters along with builders and artisans used to earn their living by building houses not only in Macedonia, but also throughout the Balkans. Activities of the Debar-Reka construction school throughout centuries have given rise to development of diverse crafts: woodcarving, architectural decoration, sculpture and stone-cutting.
6ce39e0b-ba14-5c06-b2e2-792e36cfa958.description2: The dwelling architecture in the Reka Area shows the talent and ingenuity of the anonymous native architects. The male population of this ethnic region was traditionally engaged in the construction trade. Miyak builders were widely known for their skills and distinctive architectural style in the 19th century and at the beginning of 20th century. This house was made of stone by application of bondruk system – a system of horizontal and vertical structural support beams. The usable space of the second storey has been expanded by construction of a room above the entrance area, which is supported by wooden pillars.

6d1c8ebf-40bc-511a-925c-b1e167d60a3d.name: Memo on the profits of the Suez Canal Company
6d1c8ebf-40bc-511a-925c-b1e167d60a3d.keywords: Suez Canal; Profits of the Suez Canal; Future of the Suez Canal
6d1c8ebf-40bc-511a-925c-b1e167d60a3d.description2: An important memo on the profits of the Suez Canal. It shows that the increase in average load during the last 25 years is met with an increase in net profits which are estimated to be less than five Francs per ton, although the navigation fees were much more than that amount during the period stipulated in the document. This is due to the increase in company expenses, and the company’s decision to decrease navigation fees.

6d1e302a-616b-5d9a-a46a-3a0f460f5bd5.name: Pera Palace Hotel
6d1e302a-616b-5d9a-a46a-3a0f460f5bd5.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
6d1e302a-616b-5d9a-a46a-3a0f460f5bd5.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; Ancient Istanbul; hotel; travelling
6d1e302a-616b-5d9a-a46a-3a0f460f5bd5.description2: Pera Palace Hotel was built in 1892 for the purpose of hosting the passengers of the Orient Express and was named after its location. Alexander Vallaury, a French-Turkish architect living in the city designed the hotel in a blend of neoclassical, art nouveau and oriental styles. The hotel was the first building in Turkey to be powered by electricity other than the Ottoman Palaces. It was also the only address in the city to provide hot running water for its guests and was home to the first electric elevator in Istanbul.

6dac0c9a-9cc8-5832-9efa-512fe3c88e4f.name: The Palace of Porto Trade Association Headquarters, the Arabian Room
6dac0c9a-9cc8-5832-9efa-512fe3c88e4f.history: During the siege of Porto (1832-33) by Miguelist Army led by absolutist Prince Miguel (1802-66) against the Liberal troops of his brother Prince Pedro (1798-1834), S. Francisco convent was burnt only surviving the church.  Porto Trade Association’s headquarters was erected over these ruins. Queen Maria II issued the law concession letter of 19th June 1841 to order the establishment of the Stock Exchange and the Trial Court. The solemn placing of the first stone took place on 6 October 1842.
6dac0c9a-9cc8-5832-9efa-512fe3c88e4f.keywords: Oporto; Trade Association; cultural heritage; trade; Queen Maria II; Cabralism
6dac0c9a-9cc8-5832-9efa-512fe3c88e4f.architects: Architects: Joaquim da Costa Lima (1840–1860), Gustavo Adolpho Gonçalves e Sousa (1860–1879), Thomaz Augusto Soller (1879–1883), José de Macedo Araújo Júnior (1883–1890), Joel da Silva Pereira (1894–1899) and José Marques da Silva (1889–1910); Painting and sculptures: Luigi Maninin, António Ramalho, António Carneiro, Veloso Salgado, Marques de Oliveira, Soares dos Reis, Eduardo Malta, Teixeira Lopes and Henrique Medina, among others.
6dac0c9a-9cc8-5832-9efa-512fe3c88e4f.description2: The Arabian Room (1862–1880) is considered as the most emblematic of all the Palace’s rooms, embodying the Neo-Moorish art in Portugal. Inspired by the Palace of Alhambra in Granada combines the Arab ornament grammar and the fertile imagination of the engineer/architect, Gustavo Adolpho Gonçalves e Sousa. The Hall of Nations is decorated with the national shield and the coat of arms of the countries with which Portugal had the closest ties of friendship and trade; consolidating the idea that the greatness of a nation, country or region is not a singular effort, but one of union, strength and the cooperation among people of different nations.

6dbf6cf4-1732-5bea-bb96-c766474a0193.name: *Clock tower, Beirut*
6dbf6cf4-1732-5bea-bb96-c766474a0193.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
6dbf6cf4-1732-5bea-bb96-c766474a0193.author: Stefan Weber
6dbf6cf4-1732-5bea-bb96-c766474a0193.description2: In the Ottoman provinces, clock towers became part of the urban space in the 19th century. These monuments allowed a certain control of time and symbolized "modernity". But they also functioned as imperial monuments. Beirut’s clock tower was for instance built near the Grand Serail to celebrate the anniversary of the Ottoman Sultan Abdülhamid’s [`Abd al-Hamid II]accession to the throne. So clock towers might be the most telling symbol of the presence of a new political order in the wake of the Tanzimat. Designed by Youssef Aftimus, the tower is 25 m tall, which made it the tallest piece of architecture in Beirut at the time of its completion.

6dc1ad58-0a34-56e0-8d64-e8b890165b25.name: Sayyidet al-Saha Church
6dc1ad58-0a34-56e0-8d64-e8b890165b25.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
6dc1ad58-0a34-56e0-8d64-e8b890165b25.history: This Church, inaugurated in 1898, is a made of sandstone from the coastal city of Batroun and built in a plain style, with no vaults.
6dc1ad58-0a34-56e0-8d64-e8b890165b25.description2: The church is situated close to the castle, on its southern side.

6eca5184-69aa-5866-8c8d-9b32d60fd187.name: *The gardens of the Dey's palace*
6eca5184-69aa-5866-8c8d-9b32d60fd187.archival: Lessore, E. et Wild, W., *Voyage Pittoresque dans la Régence d'Alger*, Paris: J.Delahaye, 1835.

6f1032fa-b287-57a0-81ee-3a8c6977d38a.name: The Palace of Porto Trade Association Headquarters
6f1032fa-b287-57a0-81ee-3a8c6977d38a.history: During the siege of Porto (1832-33) by Miguelist Army led by absolutist Prince Miguel (1802-66) against the Liberal troops of his brother Prince Pedro (1798-1834), S. Francisco convent was burnt only surviving the church.  Porto Trade Association’s headquarters was erected over these ruins. Queen Maria II issued the law concession letter of 19th June 1841 to order the establishment of the Stock Exchange and the Trial Court. The solemn placing of the first stone took place on 6 October 1842.
6f1032fa-b287-57a0-81ee-3a8c6977d38a.architects: Architects: Joaquim da Costa Lima (1840–1860), Gustavo Adolpho Gonçalves e Sousa (1860–1879), Thomaz Augusto Soller (1879–1883), José de Macedo Araújo Júnior (1883–1890), Joel da Silva Pereira (1894–1899) and José Marques da Silva (1889–1910); Painting and sculptures: Luigi Maninin, António Ramalho, António Carneiro, Veloso Salgado, Marques de Oliveira, Soares dos Reis, Eduardo Malta, Teixeira Lopes and Henrique Medina, among others.
6f1032fa-b287-57a0-81ee-3a8c6977d38a.description2: All the rooms of the Palácio da Bolsa are works of art, with undisputed prominence as a worthy representative of the city of Porto. Along three generations, great names in architecture, painting, sculpture and decorative arts contributed to the creation of a unique heritage at the Palácio da Bolsa, a true jewel of the neo-classical style of the 19th century. In the Palace’s interior, along with the grand architectural design of the Hall of Nations and the famous Arab Room, other noteworthy attractions include: the furniture’s symbolic meaning and its aesthetic originality; the decorative stucco’s’ intricate detail; the masterful detail of the wooden inlaid floors; the coat of arms and heraldic representations; finely sculpted statues and an immense profusion of gigantic oil paintings and frescos by great Portuguese masters.

6f83b69e-bc0a-5955-8a8f-46818fc39f26.name: *Chechia maker*
6f83b69e-bc0a-5955-8a8f-46818fc39f26.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
6f83b69e-bc0a-5955-8a8f-46818fc39f26.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
6f83b69e-bc0a-5955-8a8f-46818fc39f26.archival: Tunis au XIXe Siècle: Aquarelles et Textes de Charles Lallemand, Apollonia, 2001.
6f83b69e-bc0a-5955-8a8f-46818fc39f26.description2: This copy of a beautiful watercolour from Charles Lallemand's book *Tunis et ses Environs* shows a Tunisian artisan making a chechia. Before the competition of European industry arose in the 19th century, Tunisian artisans had been the main suppliers of the Middle East.

71d240aa-d335-59ff-8b64-aa4539d24c3b.name: *The Grand Mosque in Constanţa*
71d240aa-d335-59ff-8b64-aa4539d24c3b.description2: The Grand Mosque of Constanţa, the biggest in Romania, was built between 1910–1913 for the Muslim community of the city, on the initiative of king Carol I. It was erected on the place of a 19th century mosque, whose minbar (pulpit from where the imam delivers sermons) was preserved. The monument, a mixture of Byzantine-Egyptian and Romanian architectural elements, is the work of architect Victor Ştefănescu, who before designing it travelled to Istanbul to get acquainted with Islamic architecture. The mosque was inaugurated on 31 May 1913 in the presence of Romania’s king and queen and of Romanian and Ottoman officials. The envoy of sultan Abdul Hamid II brought a Persian rug for the mosque and awarded the orders of “Medjidie” and “Osmanieh” to Victor Ştefănescu and the city’s may.

72dcc4dd-aa26-5a94-9c71-96445ad78087.name: *The Crisis in Egypt – Panoramic View of Cairo 1882*
72dcc4dd-aa26-5a94-9c71-96445ad78087.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
72dcc4dd-aa26-5a94-9c71-96445ad78087.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
72dcc4dd-aa26-5a94-9c71-96445ad78087.description2: This expansive, panoramic engraving focuses of the Citadel of Cairo with the majestic Ottoman-style mosque erected by Muhammad Ali Pasha in memory of his son Tusun at the centre. The view is taken from high up in the Moqattam range, allowing the viewer to appreciate a panorama that takes in the wide expanse of the city of Cairo beyond the fortress, all the way to the river Nile. In composing the image, dated to 1882 CE - the year of the Anglo-Egyptian war, the artist H. W. Brewer most probably drew on contemporary photographs. Little is known about this British illustrator who specialised in depictions of cities viewed from the air.The print was issued as a supplement to The Graphic 1882. The Graphic was a British weekly illustrated newspaper, first published on 4.12.1869 by William Luson Thomas’s company Illustrated Newspapers Limited. By 1882, it had over 1000 employees. The Graphic’s influence on the art word was considerable, its readers including Vincent van Gogh.

736574db-9cd1-5e72-95d5-f1860d3596ad.name: *Mashrabiyya*
736574db-9cd1-5e72-95d5-f1860d3596ad.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
736574db-9cd1-5e72-95d5-f1860d3596ad.description2: The *mashrabiyya* is a decorative architectural element characteristic of residences in the Arab world. It was generally used on windows or balconies on the second floor or above. As well as being a natural ventilation device, the *mashrabiyya* served the purpose of shielding the occupant from the vision of passers' by, whilst still allowing natural light to pass through the gaps. This particular piece is square shaped and made of limestone, sculpted in floral patterns.

742e675b-2783-5254-a6e4-abd2e2dc3cd3.name: *Monument commemorating the installation of the Hijaz-Damascus telegraph connection, Damascus*
742e675b-2783-5254-a6e4-abd2e2dc3cd3.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
742e675b-2783-5254-a6e4-abd2e2dc3cd3.author: Stefan Weber
742e675b-2783-5254-a6e4-abd2e2dc3cd3.second_name: Constructed as the focal point of the new Ottoman urban centre at Merje square
742e675b-2783-5254-a6e4-abd2e2dc3cd3.description2: This monument is a well-known benchmark, which remained the symbol of the municipal administration until a few years ago. The bronze column in the middle of the Merje Square was erected in commemoration of the Istanbul-Damascus-Mecca telegraph link. It was the line with the sultan’s Islamist policy, acting as a symbol of the Ottoman claim to leadership over Muslims. The monumental telegraph column is crowned by a model of the Istanbul Hamidiye Mosque, where every week the Sultan ‘Abdülhamid [`Abd al-Hamid II] had his visit to the mosque for Friday prayers celebrated with an imperial march-past- a demonstration of the concentrated political power of the Sultan.

75e14725-44b8-5dc0-b587-1eba09b78832.name: Yıldız Palace Theatre
75e14725-44b8-5dc0-b587-1eba09b78832.notice: This is an unedited Database entry and may contain errors and inconsistencies in spelling. We are working to raise the funds required to complete the editing; should you wish to contribute please visit our [Support page](https://www.museumwnf.org/atrium_support.php).
75e14725-44b8-5dc0-b587-1eba09b78832.history:
Yildiz Palace, which is the last architectural example of Turkish Ottoman palace, is located on the Yildiz hill in the district of Besiktas. Sultan Ahmed I was the first to build a pavilion, over this land registered at the time to the Private treasury of the Ottoman Sultan as a hunting place sultans beginning during the reign of Suleiman the Magnificent (1520-1566).  
The main construction in the palace started in the period of Sultan Abdulhamid II (1876-1909) and it was called Saray-i Humayun (Central palace). During this period the palace comprised of buildings for private use of the sultan as well as buildings, allocated for the officials, repair shops and carpentry like repairing shop, carpenter’s shop and the buildings of culture and art such as theatre, museum and library. The Palace begun to serve as a museum under the name of Directorate of the Museum of Yildiz Palace since 1993.
75e14725-44b8-5dc0-b587-1eba09b78832.description2: This is the only palace theatre that can be seen today. It was built by the Sultan Abdulhamid II for the visit of German Imperial Kaiser Wilhem II, together with the Shale Kiosk in 1899. Three walls of the theatre hall, of a small rectangular plan, are surrounded by the boxes carried by columns. The box that faced the stage belonged to the sultan. The walls were decorated with hand-drawn and the ceiling was endowed with gold star patterns on the blue ground. Oil paintings are hung around the stage. In addition to performer groups consisting of Italian and Turkish artists, foreign theatre groups visiting Istanbul and some local artists were also occasionally allowed to the palace. Among them, there were French artists, Sarah Bernhardt and Coquelain Cadet and Russian singer Feodor Chaliapin, local artists Gullu Agop Efendi and Nashit Efendi. In the theatre the operas such as Barber of Sevil, Norma, Rigoletto, Traviata, Carmen and Aida were put on stage. The original wardrobes representing the period of use are exhibited in a section of the theatre.

7625cc1a-04cd-541e-97b3-01fa3eac5fdf.name: *Dolmabahçe Palace Portal Under Construction*
7625cc1a-04cd-541e-97b3-01fa3eac5fdf.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
7625cc1a-04cd-541e-97b3-01fa3eac5fdf.keywords: Dolmabahçe Palace; Ottoman architecture; close-up from Dolmahçe Palace portal
7625cc1a-04cd-541e-97b3-01fa3eac5fdf.description2: Lacan heaps particular praise on the artist's panorama taken from Beyazıt Tower as well as on his photograph of the architectural elements of Galata Tower, the Hagia Sophia, the Mosque of Sultan Ahmed I, and Dolmabahçe Sarayı. Robertson’s Istanbul photographs are concerned primarily with the city’s historical monuments. They reveal the city’s magnificent Byzantine and Ottoman structures from different angles and with close-ups taken in an approach that is usually quite aesthetic.

76457a6e-00a0-52e0-a869-4eec84837b92.name: Photograph of the Old Railway Station in Skopje
76457a6e-00a0-52e0-a869-4eec84837b92.holder: Museum of the City of Skopje
76457a6e-00a0-52e0-a869-4eec84837b92.author: Zoja Bogdanovska, historian, Museum of the City of Skopje
76457a6e-00a0-52e0-a869-4eec84837b92.keywords: Railroad; railway; railway station; Ottoman Balkans
76457a6e-00a0-52e0-a869-4eec84837b92.third_name: Fotografija na starata zeleznichka stanica vo Skopje
76457a6e-00a0-52e0-a869-4eec84837b92.description2: The first railroad in Macedonia was the track running from Thessalonica via Skopje to Belgrade. Its construction was financed with foreign investments and began in 1871. The track to Skopje was finished in 1873. The Skopje-Mitrovica railway line was completed in 1878. In 1888, it was connected to Serbian railways at the border crossing Zibevche near Vranje.

78eecb65-6040-5c83-8995-b8c35cb4d3a6.name: Nusretiye Mosque and Tophane Square
78eecb65-6040-5c83-8995-b8c35cb4d3a6.keywords: Photograph; Old İstanbul Photograph; İstanbul; James Robertson
78eecb65-6040-5c83-8995-b8c35cb4d3a6.description2: James Robertson arrived in Istanbul in 1840 and started work as head etcher in Ottoman Mint. He began taking photos of Istanbul soon after. There was previously a mosque located on the site of the current Mosque, which was known as the Mosque of the Artillery Barracks (Tophane-i Amire Arabacilar Kislasi Camii) built by Selim III (1789-1807). When that mosque was destroyed by the Firuzaga fire, the Nusretiye Mosque, located on Meclis-i Mebusan Street in the Tophane District of Beyoglu, was built on the order of Sultan Mahmud (1784-1839), and was constructed by the Krikor Amira Balyan. The construction lasted from 1823 to 1826 and was broadly restored between the years of 1955 and 1958, and partially again between 1980 and 1992. While its architecture is influenced by Islamic elements, it retains a Baroque style, making it unique to the city.

7a05190e-1927-5037-ba2d-10e15038ab09.name: Dar al-Makina
7a05190e-1927-5037-ba2d-10e15038ab09.history: Built under the auspices of Sultan al-Hasan I in 1890, this impressive factory building is located in the west of Fez at al-Michour Jedid. One of the most important works of this Sultan in the royal city of Fez, which was constructed for the production of weapons in cooperation with the Italians.
7a05190e-1927-5037-ba2d-10e15038ab09.keywords: Factory; industry; Italian industrialists; Italians in Morocco; Italians in North Africa; migration; work; urban changes; city; urban space; Moroccan city; Islamic city; traditional city; changes in urban space; urban planning; plan; European architecture; European influence; artistic exchanges; war; weapons; arms; protectorate; industrialisation
