b5762c66-bf5b-5b77-bfe4-6c9e135ce487.artist_birthplace: David Roberts: Edinburgh, Scotland; Louis Hague: Tournai, Belgium
b5762c66-bf5b-5b77-bfe4-6c9e135ce487.artist_deathplace: David Roberts: London; Louis Hague: London

b5eeac6a-d016-5d9a-8a53-0fd0bd897372.name: Excavation of l'Avenue de l'Opéra and Boulevard Henri IV
b5eeac6a-d016-5d9a-8a53-0fd0bd897372.description2: When Napoléon III wanted a new opera house to be built (l’Opéra Garnier), he asked Haussmann to excavate the road beneath it, allowing him to go to the opera safely and without risk of being attacked from his residence at the Château des Tuileries. Haussman was forced to dig through an old neighbourhood, built on a hill. This photograph indicates the vastness of the works. The architect Garnier ordered Haussman to ensure no trees blocked the view of the opera house.

b6880f81-b97a-53a0-8afb-78259cca0821.name: Dolmabahçe Palace
b6880f81-b97a-53a0-8afb-78259cca0821.description: The admiration the Ottoman sultans had for Western monarchs, resulted in the construction of new palaces on the banks of the Bosphorus.

b7084bd4-c4a5-5fd8-b3d4-f24093a3a2c3.name: Fiat garage and showroom
b7084bd4-c4a5-5fd8-b3d4-f24093a3a2c3.history: Constructed in 1919, according to a design by Italian architect Aldo Manassi in the Mers Sultan district, the building represents one of the world’s most prolific automotive companies, which began trading in Morocco in 1919.
b7084bd4-c4a5-5fd8-b3d4-f24093a3a2c3.keywords: Art deco; applied arts; classicism; pilaster; floral motifs; decoration; applied arts; geometrical motifs; zellij; ceramic; European influence; Italians in Morocco; Italians in North Africa; Italian architects in Morocco; migration; work; technical innovation; transportation; car; industry; Italian industries; Italian industrialists; FIAT; trade; commerce; city; European architecture; plan; Moroccan city; Casablanca; urban planning; colonial city; urban space; changes in urban spaces
b7084bd4-c4a5-5fd8-b3d4-f24093a3a2c3.description2: The building consists of two floors, the ground-floor designed to accommodate a garage and exhibition hall. Art Deco in style, classical-style pilasters reach up to the first floor and terminate in decorative floral mouldings. The inner detailing surrounds windows that are topped with decorated mouldings with a similar floral theme. Two arched windows, with small balconies, are topped by shallow porches. Two medallions, which bear the name “Fiat” in deep blue, highlight the protruding facade.

b9ee7653-5f89-5cc9-b8cc-d6b70b1e48ce.name: Izmir Clock Tower
b9ee7653-5f89-5cc9-b8cc-d6b70b1e48ce.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
b9ee7653-5f89-5cc9-b8cc-d6b70b1e48ce.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; Ancient İzmir; Tower
b9ee7653-5f89-5cc9-b8cc-d6b70b1e48ce.description2: The clock tower was designed by the Levantine French architect Raymond Charles Père and built in 1901 to commemorate the 25th anniversary of Abdülhamid II's accession to the throne (reigned 1876-1909). The clock itself was a gift from German Emperor Wilhelm II (reigned 1888-1918). It is decorated in an elaborate Ottoman architecture style.

baca824e-062d-5426-b385-13a5074e8755.name: View of Livorno from the Lighthouse. On the right, one can see the so-called 'Turkish graveyard' highlighted in green
baca824e-062d-5426-b385-13a5074e8755.author: Daniela Tazzi
baca824e-062d-5426-b385-13a5074e8755.third_name: *Panorama della città e contorni di Livorno disegnata dal Fanale*
baca824e-062d-5426-b385-13a5074e8755.description2: In 1762, Muslims living in Livorno were granted a plot of land outside the city walls, near the beach, to build a graveyard (highlighted in green in the lithography). The graveyard remained in use until the second half of the 19th century. A Muslim graveyard existed in Livorno even before the 18th century. A significant Muslim community lived in town. Its first members were captives taken to Italy as slaves. Muslim traders settled in town as well. In 1856, the graveyard was enlarged and surrounded by walls. In 1872 it was demolished to build a road and some of the graves were moved to the city graveyard.
baca824e-062d-5426-b385-13a5074e8755.holding_institution_org: Biblioteca Labronica F. D. Guerrazzi Livorno

bb7e5c73-80d2-53d1-8bb0-be2895feb51b.name: *The European neighbourhood of Tunis and the Northern Suburbs*
bb7e5c73-80d2-53d1-8bb0-be2895feb51b.author: Patrizia Pampana
bb7e5c73-80d2-53d1-8bb0-be2895feb51b.third_name: *Quartiere europeo e sobborgo di Sugga, parte settentrionale di Tunisi*
bb7e5c73-80d2-53d1-8bb0-be2895feb51b.description2: An early photograph of a view of Tunis, the picture shows in the European neighbourbood. It was taken on a trip to Tunisia organised by the Italian Geographical Society (Società geografica italiana) in 1875.

en: Bonetti, Maria Francesca, and Mancini, Maria (eds), *Tunisia 1875. La spedizione della Società geografica italiana nelle immagini di Lodovico Tuminello*, Rome: Società geografica italiana, 2007.

bb9dad9b-d6d3-5823-9949-97ec2cba42f3.name: Centrally planned collective housing
bb9dad9b-d6d3-5823-9949-97ec2cba42f3.description: This centrally planned house is an example of a style of collective housing, dating back to the 1850s. This type of house is built around a central space to be used collectively by all the building's inhabitants. The separate houses, generally inhabited by families, were also built around this open space.
bb9dad9b-d6d3-5823-9949-97ec2cba42f3.author: Jeff El-Msanne, David Andos
bb9dad9b-d6d3-5823-9949-97ec2cba42f3.history: This style of collective housing emerged alongside other styles (such as the monocellular house or the courtyard house) in the 1850s, a period which is generally considered to be the peak of Ottoman rule in the region. The desire for more economically viable and sociable housing were the main reasons behind its success.

bbeb7fe5-88d9-5182-83a9-e637b3a17a0b.name: Tile panel
bbeb7fe5-88d9-5182-83a9-e637b3a17a0b.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
bbeb7fe5-88d9-5182-83a9-e637b3a17a0b.keywords: Ceramic; earthenware; collection; collector; vegetal decoration; ceramic tile; tilework; tile panel; Iznik; Ottoman ceramic; revival
bbeb7fe5-88d9-5182-83a9-e637b3a17a0b.materials: Slip-covered and hand-painted in various colours and glazed, on earthenware blanks
bbeb7fe5-88d9-5182-83a9-e637b3a17a0b.description2:
The architect of Membland Hall in Devon commissioned this sumptuous design for bathroom tiles from William Morris. Morris had the tiles painted in the studios of William de Morgan (1839-1917). They represent a rare collaboration between these two creative geniuses.  
Edward Charles Baring, 1st Baron Revelstoke, was the builder of Membland Hall. He was a merchant banker. The hall was later demolished.

bc05121b-1942-54f8-ba62-84b29282f089.name: Tile Panel
bc05121b-1942-54f8-ba62-84b29282f089.description2: Kütahya was the second most important ceramic production centre after İznik due to the rich clay deposits in the area. Although there was a decline in ceramic production at the beginning of the 19th century, in the last quarter of that same century production was revived and new designs inspired by İznik ceramics were produced.

bc605726-30eb-5689-b5fe-e1831e32d41b.name: Central Market
bc605726-30eb-5689-b5fe-e1831e32d41b.history: Built in 1917 according to a design by French architect Pierre Bousquet, the organisation of shops into galleries is in harmony with the Moroccan market or *suq* tradition. Furthermore, it highlights the economic activity of Casablanca at the time of the French Protectorate.
bc605726-30eb-5689-b5fe-e1831e32d41b.keywords: French in Morocco; French in North Africa; French architects in North Africa; Suq; covered market; covered suq; traditional city; city; Islamic city; Islamic urban space; Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic architecture in Morocco; Islamic influence; French in Morocco; protectorate; traditional building; plan; Moroccan city; urban planning; colonial architecture; applied arts; vegetal motifs; zellij; ceramic; geometrical motifs; trade; economy; commerce; work; public space
bc605726-30eb-5689-b5fe-e1831e32d41b.description2: This space is in keeping with traditional Moroccan market structures, wherein different types of shops are grouped in galleries. The main monumental gate, which provides access to the market on Avenue Mohammad V, is surmounted by a horseshoe arch richly decorated with traditional figurative motifs (vegetal tracery) and predominantly green polychrome *zellige* (mosaic tilework). The corners of the structure are softened by two small arched valances or *lambrequins*. At the top of the gate there is a small canopy furnished with green tiles.

bd591c95-bb06-5105-b1bd-b95187ad7a88.name: Villa Maria, in Tunis, the mansion of Luigi Rey, the son of a migrant from Piedmont (Italy)
bd591c95-bb06-5105-b1bd-b95187ad7a88.dates: Photograph: first years of the 20th century; building: late 19th century
bd591c95-bb06-5105-b1bd-b95187ad7a88.author: Giulia Barrera
bd591c95-bb06-5105-b1bd-b95187ad7a88.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906, p. 44
bd591c95-bb06-5105-b1bd-b95187ad7a88.third_name: *Villa Maria del cav. Luigi Rey, imprenditore*
bd591c95-bb06-5105-b1bd-b95187ad7a88.description2: Luigi Rey was the son of Italian immigrants Giuseppe Rey (1808-1897), of Piedmont and Adelaide Baldacci, of Tuscany. In 1836, Giuseppe Rey was dispatched to Tunis by his employer, a construction company from Genoa, to work in the Bardo Palace (the official residence of the Bey of Tunis). After completing the contract Giuseppe decided to stay in Tunisia, where he continued to work at the service of the Bey. Together with his three children (Luigi, Antonio and Pio), Giuseppe Rey set up a construction company that continued after his death. Predominantly with his brothers but at times on his own, Luigi Rey built a variety of private and public edifices, including the Tunisia Palace Hotel (designed by architect Resplandy).

en: Finzi, Silvia (ed.), *Architectures italiennes de Tunisie/Architetture italiane di Tunisia*, Tunis: Finzi/Ambasciata d'Italia, 2002.

bd5974b2-add3-5352-9473-20bfa7b6d015.name: Beiteddine Palace
bd5974b2-add3-5352-9473-20bfa7b6d015.description: The construction of the palace took ten years. Celebrated Lebanese constructors, such as Rustam and Yusuf Mujahes from Shuwayr were employed, as well as a number of European engineers and architects invited by the Prince Bashir al-Shihabi. Tiles were also imported from celebrated masters in Istanbul, Aleppo and Damascus.
bd5974b2-add3-5352-9473-20bfa7b6d015.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Hassan El Masri, Remy Nader
bd5974b2-add3-5352-9473-20bfa7b6d015.history:
A tile framework imported from Marseille was added to this palace at the beginning of Prince Bashir al-Shihabi's reign resembling the typical Lebanese house, a future national symbol. The palace is interesting, as the ornamentation shows clear influences from the late Ottoman architecture, whereas the façade contains more neoclassical (or late baroque) elements from the late 19th and early 20th centuries. These additions did not alter the basic structure of the building, however. Ways the structure of this palace differed notably from the traditional models include: the location of a central stair inside the main hall, rather than outside, and the transformation of the patio into a public space between the palace and the street.  
Beiteddine palace was built to replace the palace at Deir al-Qamar, which had become too small for the expanding number of soldiers and servants. The prince ordered a luxurious palace to be built on the hill overlooking Deir al-Qamar, on land he had bought upon his marriage to "Sitt al-Shams.”

bd610f90-dbc3-5a38-87c0-75bb5979c752.name: House of Mohammed Ali
bd610f90-dbc3-5a38-87c0-75bb5979c752.holder: IMARET – Institute Mohammed Ali for the Research of the Eastern Tradition (under contract with the Egyptian Waqf Organization)
bd610f90-dbc3-5a38-87c0-75bb5979c752.author: I.M.A.R.E.T.
bd610f90-dbc3-5a38-87c0-75bb5979c752.history: According to local tradition, the building was the house of the local representative of the Ottoman administration or, later, the house of Mohammed Ali, founder of modern Egypt, who was born in Kavala in 1769. An inscription erected outside the house in 1883, almost 35 years after Mohammed Ali’s death, states that the building is among his charitable works, together with Imaret. It seems therefore possible that Mohammed Ali acquired the house, the finest one in town, and made it part of his Waqf, on the occasion of his visit to Kavala on his way back to Egypt from his only visit to Istanbul (August 1846). Currently, the House operates as a Museum and the seat of I.M.A.R.E.T. - Institute Mohammed Ali for the Research of the Eastern Tradition.
bd610f90-dbc3-5a38-87c0-75bb5979c752.keywords: 18th century Ottoman vernacular architecture; male and female quarters (selâmlik and haremlik); Mohammed Ali; Egypt
bd610f90-dbc3-5a38-87c0-75bb5979c752.description2: The House of Mohammed ‘Ali is a typical example of the so-called ‘broad-fronted, two-floor traditional dwelling’ with a row of rooms leading to the main living area on the first floor and a covered courtyard on the ground floor. Today, it is the only remaining example of vernacular architecture from the Ottoman period in the Balkan area, which still preserves the distinction between the male (Selâmlık) and female (Haremlik) quarters.

bdc77deb-d803-5076-89a4-a826a7e730aa.name: The stand of the Italian Community in Tunisia at the International Exhibition held in Turin in 1911
bdc77deb-d803-5076-89a4-a826a7e730aa.author: Massimo Sanacore, Giulia Barrera
bdc77deb-d803-5076-89a4-a826a7e730aa.archival: ASLi, Archivio Moreno di Tunisi, b. 15
bdc77deb-d803-5076-89a4-a826a7e730aa.description2:
The picture shows how, on the occasion of the 1911 international exhibition in Turin the Italian community in Tunisia chose to represent itself by blending elements taken from the Italian and from the Tunisian material culture.  
One can read the sign E. & A. Coen, Tunisi, Susa, Sfax. Eugenio and Alfredo Coen were the owners of a furniture factory and of the imposing furniture shop, “Au Palais Arabe”, in downtown Tunis.

be01848b-7ea6-50bc-b6b0-fc23630b1bfd.name: Casablanca: local inhabitants rebuilding their city
be01848b-7ea6-50bc-b6b0-fc23630b1bfd.description2: Casablanca was host to many French architectural experiments, and became a model for urban planners worldwide. Marshall Hubert Lyautey called on Henri Prost (1874–1859) to direct architectural works in the French Protectorate of Morocco. Thus, Prost established new plans for the cities of Casablanca, Rabat, Fez, Meknes, and Marrakesh. He decided to build a "new French-style city" in Casablanca. This photograph shows the works at the junction between the old medina and the new quarter at the same height as the old clocktower, with a caption stressing the "Arab population's" contribution to the works.

bf3b00b7-e2b1-52d9-ac3a-710b848a0c69.name: Medal – The construction of the Suez Canal
bf3b00b7-e2b1-52d9-ac3a-710b848a0c69.artist:
Eugène André Oudiné (1st January 1810, Paris – 12 April 1887, Paris);  
Alexis Joseph Depaulis (30 August 1792, Paris – 29 September 1867, Paris)
bf3b00b7-e2b1-52d9-ac3a-710b848a0c69.description2: Built between 1859–1869, the Suez Canal represents a direct link between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea. It had a positive influence on the commerce of Europe with the southern Arabian Peninsula, as it significantly reduced the duration of transports, given that in the past a longer route, which went around Africa, was used. This bronze medal dedicated to the construction of the canal was issued in 1864. Its obverse, designed by Chaplain, features the laureate head of emperor Napoleon III. On the reverse, designed by Depaulis, is depicted Industria standing between Europe and Africa, who are holding hands. Above the three female figures is inscribed “Jonction des deux mers” (Junction of the two seas) and beyond there are emblems of Egypt (a pyramid, the Sphinx, a palm tree) and of the canal (a ship).

bf7b0320-6a5a-5d4b-924a-eaaf6be147cf.name: Sakan house
bf7b0320-6a5a-5d4b-924a-eaaf6be147cf.description: This house is built on a principle of scalability, allowing the house to grow as the family expands, for example, without affecting its internal logic. Many of these houses can still be seen in Médawwar-Rmeil, Beirut, today. They are seen as 'heritage' houses, and are associated with the "triple arched" houses, which use the same fundamental basis. Many have been incorporated into the structure of new modern houses, coating the walls in concrete to create a new building and hiding the old *sakan* inside its very structure. The new, remodelled *sakan* can be identified today by its door, which overlooks/opens onto the main hallway and central shared room. The outdoor spaces in these houses are still built on the traditional model.
bf7b0320-6a5a-5d4b-924a-eaaf6be147cf.author: Jeff El-Msanne, David Andos
bf7b0320-6a5a-5d4b-924a-eaaf6be147cf.history: This type of house was generally a rural habitation until the 1950s. Today, it is part of the urban fabric of many towns, sandwiched between other properties on often narrow streets, or attached to new, modern builds.

bfe37257-aff0-5289-b8c5-59ecbe78ace2.name: Yıldız Palace Greenhouse Kiosk
bfe37257-aff0-5289-b8c5-59ecbe78ace2.notice: This is an unedited Database entry and may contain errors and inconsistencies in spelling. We are working to raise the funds required to complete the editing; should you wish to contribute please visit our [Support page](https://www.museumwnf.org/atrium_support.php).
bfe37257-aff0-5289-b8c5-59ecbe78ace2.history:
Yildiz Palace, which is the last architectural example of Turkish Ottoman palace, is located on the Yildiz hill in the district of Beşiktaş. Sultan Ahmed I was the first to build a pavilion, over this land registered at the time to the Private treasury of the Ottoman Sultan as a hunting place sultans beginning during the reign of Suleiman the Magnificent (1520-1566).  
The main construction in the palace started in the period of Sultan Abdulhamid II (1876-1909) and it was called Saray-i Humayun (Central palace). During this period the palace comprised of buildings for private use of the sultan as well as buildings, allocated for the officials, repair shops and carpentry like repairing shop, carpenter’s shop and the buildings of culture and art such as theatre, museum and library. The Palace begun to serve as a museum under the name of "Directorate of the Museum of Yildiz Palace" since 1993.
bfe37257-aff0-5289-b8c5-59ecbe78ace2.description2:
The palace has an inner garden which is called “Hasbahce” with a pool inside resembling a natural creek. In different points of this garden there are small independent resort kiosks.  
In the Palace garden winter gardens and greenhouses were constructed for growing plants appropriate for the natural topography. Some greenhouses had unique designs where then-fashionable iron and glass elements were expertly used and it is known some of them had been heated. Especially the Limonluk Köşkü, designed by Raimondo D’Aronco and found just behing the Harem Gate is one of the most distinguished structures in the Palace.

c0dbe8f9-c861-5074-9fb8-b7dfcde583ed.name: *Al Azhar University, Cairo*
c0dbe8f9-c861-5074-9fb8-b7dfcde583ed.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
c0dbe8f9-c861-5074-9fb8-b7dfcde583ed.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
c0dbe8f9-c861-5074-9fb8-b7dfcde583ed.description2: Ludwig Deutsch  (1855-1935) was an Austrian-Jewish Orientalist painter. Here he tries to capture the atmosphere within the courtyard of the Al-Azhar mosque, first built in the 10th century and a major religious, intellectual and political hub of activity ever since. One of the oldest and most revered universities in the Islamic world, it was from here that a revolt against French troops was launched in 1798.  The French general Kleber was assassinated by Suleiman al Halabi, an al Azhar student, and later, Al Azhar was a focal point of protest against the Ottoman occupation of Egypt. Despite Deutsch's near-photographic style, his depiction is not entirely accurate and contains several errors: the arcades under the wooden oriel - their arches in reality wider and squatter - were not blocked up in his time, and the colour of the stonework is exaggerated. The praying men in the background are facing in the wrong direction (the direction of prayer or qibla in fact being to their right), Finally, the tall dark figure in the centre of the painting clutches what appears to be a Holy Qur'an between his dirty shoes, an act any Muslim would consider an absolute sacrilege.

c3469ef6-684c-5443-94aa-94ce360bb640.name: House
c3469ef6-684c-5443-94aa-94ce360bb640.dates: End of 19th – beginning of the 20th century
c3469ef6-684c-5443-94aa-94ce360bb640.author: Prof. Petar Namichev (PhD)
c3469ef6-684c-5443-94aa-94ce360bb640.history: *Tajfas* were very well organized and had extremely professional approach to their work. These construction masters developed a secret construction language which they used for communication among themselves. There were even variants of the secret construction language, depending on the local dialects and the origin of the members of the *tajfa*. The best known artists of the woodcarving craft in Macedonia came from the Reka Area, including Makarija Frchkovski, Petre Filipovski Garkata and his brother Marko Filipovski – as well as many others.
c3469ef6-684c-5443-94aa-94ce360bb640.description2: The construction trade has an exceptionally long tradition in the Reka Area. The artisan school in the Debar-Reka area, with its centre in Galichnik, was mentioned in sources from as early as the 10th century. People from this area – the Miyaks – have given birth to numerous generations of construction masters throughout the centuries. Construction *tajfas* from the Reka Area were widely known and used to build houses, churches, mosques and other structures throughout the Balkans, even in Asia Minor. This three-storey house was built completely of stone. It is the type of tower house of asymmetrical lay out distinctive to the Reka Area. Construction of tower houses developed in this area for the purpose of defence and protection from intruders in the turbulent times of the 18th and 19th centuries.

c4322598-8028-5f79-ae2e-c4ce254ee9ee.name: Military Infirmary
c4322598-8028-5f79-ae2e-c4ce254ee9ee.description: This hospital (or *hastahane* in Ottoman Turkish), commissioned by Sultan 'Abd al-'Aziz (Abdülaziz) (1861-76) in 1865, was often referred to as the military infirmary. The building included two wings, and the northern wing housed a drugstore (*ajzah*). The courthouse which later inhabited the building was moved to a different location when it became the Lebanese University's Institute of Fine Arts.
c4322598-8028-5f79-ae2e-c4ce254ee9ee.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
c4322598-8028-5f79-ae2e-c4ce254ee9ee.history: In 1865, this military hospital was commissioned by the Ottoman sultan 'Abd al-'Aziz (Abdülaziz).The hospital was later converted to a courthouse by the French, who took control of the city in 1918 following the collapse of the Ottoman Empire. Today, the building houses the Lebanese University's Institute of Fine Arts.
c4322598-8028-5f79-ae2e-c4ce254ee9ee.keywords: Infirmary; Sultan Abdul Aziz; Military; Hospital

c4e1a5f3-c276-5476-bae6-589764a31420.name: House
c4e1a5f3-c276-5476-bae6-589764a31420.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Prof. Marula Nikoloska, Ph.D. (consultant)
c4e1a5f3-c276-5476-bae6-589764a31420.history: Krushevo houses had to be adjusted to the naturally steep terrain on which they sit. The dwelling architecture of this town thus shows notable vertical development, which has given rise to creative architectural solutions for the purpose of maximum use of space.
c4e1a5f3-c276-5476-bae6-589764a31420.description2: The architecture of Krushevo was influenced by houses in Moscopole, as well as by the mountain dwellings in Epirus and Thessaly. Native architects, Vlachs originating from Moscopole and Miyaks from the Reka Area, created their distinctive and highly autonomous dwelling architecture which combined the traditional mode of building with architectural solutions arising from the steep terrain. This house is a three-storied structure of symmetrical type. The ground floor is made of stone and mortar. Upper stories were built of wooden framing and adobe, covered with plaster. The dynamic rhythm of the front façade has been achieved by the repetitive layout of windows and balconies above the front door at the second and third storey. The decoration is enhanced by the intricate wooden and iron balcony balusters on the second and third storey.

c5d82e4f-8d74-5430-90f9-57dd3f2fea11.name: Section of a Roman triumphal arch
c5d82e4f-8d74-5430-90f9-57dd3f2fea11.archival: Ravoisié, A., *Exploration scientifique de l'Algérie pendant les annéees 1840-1841-1842*, vol. I, Paris: 1846.

c7de3940-ac44-5e99-93fd-416c7b6e83ea.name: Ihlamur Pavilion
c7de3940-ac44-5e99-93fd-416c7b6e83ea.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
c7de3940-ac44-5e99-93fd-416c7b6e83ea.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; Ancient Istanbul; palace; pavilion
c7de3940-ac44-5e99-93fd-416c7b6e83ea.description2: The Ihlamur Pavilion is located at the intersection of Nüzhetiye Street between Ihlamur and Tesvikiye and has an area of about 25,000 square meters. The Ihlamur Pavilion consists of two kiosks: the Maiyet and Merasim Kiosk. The Merasim Kiosk was reserved for the sultan’s personal use. The Maiyet Kiosk, the simpler of the two, was used by the sultan’s entourage and family members, and it currently serves as a beautiful cafeteria. The kiosk is decorated with crystal chandeliers, European-style furniture, Hereke carpets, and decorated vases.

cab1d1b6-5bd0-5d68-aaf4-36e8d7c863e4.name: *View of Smyrna*
cab1d1b6-5bd0-5d68-aaf4-36e8d7c863e4.author: Papastratos 1990, vol. 2, 578-79, figs. 617-18; Delivorrias, Fotopoulos 1997, 508-9, figs. 900-901
cab1d1b6-5bd0-5d68-aaf4-36e8d7c863e4.description2: Both this print and the *View of Constantinople* are based on earlier Western ones, which have been assimilated into the distinctive Athonite topographical style. They are exceptions to the corpus of Athonite prints, since they are of secular subjects. The printmaker was, indeed, active outside Athos, where he executed nonreligious commissions. The subjects relate to the tradition of topographical murals depicting important commercial and cultural centers of the day that decorated the mansions of wealthy merchants by the mid-eighteenth century. Kaldis aimed to supply a wider public with inexpensive works of a decorative nature. The activity of merchants from Lesbos at Smyrna, Constantinople, and the Black Sea on the one hand justified the choice of subject and, on the other, provided the appropriate network in which the multiple printed works could circulate. In order to attract the largest possible clientele, the view is coloured.

en: Delivorrias, Angelos, and Fotopoulos, Dionisis, *Greece at the Benaki Museum*, Athens: Benaki Museum, 1997.
Papastratos, Dory, *Paper Icons: Greek Orthodox Religious Engravings, 1665–1899*, vol. 2, Athens: Papastratos, 1990.

cafcd6e4-6930-5d23-8538-b552e0f9216e.name: Hôtel Majestic
cafcd6e4-6930-5d23-8538-b552e0f9216e.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
cafcd6e4-6930-5d23-8538-b552e0f9216e.history: This was the first luxury or grand hotel in Tunis. Built in 1912 and designed by the architect Paul Baron in an Art Nouveau style, in the early 20th century the Hôtel Majestic was the best hotel around. It was requisitioned by the German army between November 1942 and May 1943 and became the seat first of the Kommanduntur, then, after liberation, of the American army headquarters. After Tunisian independence and until the mid sixties President Habib Bourguiba used the hotel to receive many foreign heads of states and official guests. Many famous foreign artists, such as Brasser, Barbara, Aznavour, Luis Marino and Bécaud, who had come to Tunisia to give concerts or recitals, also stayed in the Hôtel Majestic.
cafcd6e4-6930-5d23-8538-b552e0f9216e.description2: Located on Avenue de Paris, the Hôtel Majestic offered, from a decorative and structural point of view, something totally new. With its sunny façade and terrace, this four-storey building was the first of its kind in the city. The furniture, woodwork, lighting and the rooms, which opened out onto one another in a modern fashion, were what gave the hotel its charm.

cb50db24-36a3-5378-b0e6-e03a650cef9b.name: Tourbet el Bey
cb50db24-36a3-5378-b0e6-e03a650cef9b.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
cb50db24-36a3-5378-b0e6-e03a650cef9b.history: The Tourbet El Bey monument is Tunisia's largest and most famous royal mausoleum from Ottoman or Husainid times, notable for its architecture and exterior, as well as for its size and number of cupolas and tombs. It was built by 'Ali Pacha Bey II, the fourth bey of the Hussainid dynasty, around 1770. A *kouttab*, a *sabil*, and a large *madrasa* were also founded in association with this mausoleum. This necropolis for the Beys of Tunis holds the tombs of the Husainids and their families, as well as those of a few important members of the nobility or loyal servants and ministers.
cb50db24-36a3-5378-b0e6-e03a650cef9b.keywords: Architecture; Andalusian style; Italian style; stucco; necropolis
cb50db24-36a3-5378-b0e6-e03a650cef9b.description2:
This funerary complex, composed of eight spacious rooms, is set around two courtyards, one surrounded by porticos and another open-air. The rooms and patios contain the tombs of 165 different beys who had governed Tunis from 1759 to 1942. The room for the ruling beys is notable for by its Arab-style cupolas, similar to those in the Sidi Mahrez Mosque.  
A second room is covered by a barrel vault - unique to Tunisia - decorated with wonderfully carved stuccos. The walls, on the other hand, are decorated in an Italian style with slabs of coloured stone or marble marquetery. The rooms are all decorated with faience ceramics, which are evidence of this necropolis' European and Arab influences as they were both imported from Europe and locally produced. This monument-cum-museum houses one of the most important collections of funerary inscriptions.

cbffe8c2-7457-5662-8cc7-208d2edc343c.name: The English Consulate (Ruins)
cbffe8c2-7457-5662-8cc7-208d2edc343c.author: Giulia Barrera
cbffe8c2-7457-5662-8cc7-208d2edc343c.second_name: The ruins of the English Consulate in Alexandria (Egypt) after the bombing of the city by the British Navy in 1882
cbffe8c2-7457-5662-8cc7-208d2edc343c.description2:
The author of this picture, Luigi Fiorillo, was an Italian photographer who migrated to Alexandria (Egypt) around 1870 and opened a successful photography shop. In 1877, he participated as photographer in an expedition to Shewa region (Ethiopia), organised by the Italian Geographical Society, and ten years later in an Italian military expedition for the colonial conquest of Eritrea.  
In 1882, Fiorillo was one of the few Europeans who remained in Alexandria after the anti-foreign rioting and documented the consequences of the British bombardment on Alexandria of July 11th. He collected 50 pictures of the city ruins in an album titled “Souvenir d'Alexandrie: Ruines, 1882”.  
On the back of some photos that he took in the 1880s, Fiorillo defines himself as “le photographe de Son Altesse le Prince Mohammed Toussoun Pasha” (the photographer of his Majesty Prince Mohammed Toussoun Pasha). Luigi Fiorillo died in 1898.

en: Silingardi, Adriano, ”Luigi Fiorillo, l’avventuroso fotografo di Alessandria d’Egitto”, unpublished paper (available on line) for the exhibition of the same name, Genoa, 2014.

cc27cb2b-74b2-53c7-99e4-842dcfe24334.name: The post office
cc27cb2b-74b2-53c7-99e4-842dcfe24334.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
cc27cb2b-74b2-53c7-99e4-842dcfe24334.history: Following the establishment of the French Protectorate in Tunisia, the French administration set up the post and telegraphy service in the Regency of Tunis. The post and telegraph office was created on 1 July 1888. The first Tunisian stamp was issued the following day. Finally, the Hôtel des Postes de Tunis was opened on the 11 July 1882. The first telegraph lines connecting Tunis and Marseille were soon built, and the first international communication was effectuated in November 1915 between Tunisia and Algeria.
cc27cb2b-74b2-53c7-99e4-842dcfe24334.description2: The Hôtel des PTT was designed by the architect Henri Saladin, and built on the Rue d'Italie (now called Rue Charles-de-Gaulle) in a network of straight roads lined with apartment blocks. This imposing building is designed in a Greco-Roman style. The windowless arches and huge wall clock on the main façade hint to the enormous dimensions of this municipal building's great hall. It was listed as a historic monument in 1992.

cca20edd-41d0-541f-a5ca-f482c3ebc627.name: *The Continental Hotel*
cca20edd-41d0-541f-a5ca-f482c3ebc627.keywords: Hotel; Landmarks of Egypt; Old Hotels; Tourism
cca20edd-41d0-541f-a5ca-f482c3ebc627.description2: The Continental Hotel, one of Cairo’s most important hotels, where many historic meetings were held and kings and presidents stayed.

ccab83d9-f7e5-548c-8ca6-04c897269224.name: Tile fragment of the Omar Mosque in Jerusalem
ccab83d9-f7e5-548c-8ca6-04c897269224.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art
ccab83d9-f7e5-548c-8ca6-04c897269224.description2: Islamic art collected by the Museum of Applied Arts.

cd6b2c88-0a74-5d2f-8cba-5b3ea7174b9c.name: Tympanum made of 16 tiles from the palace of the grand vizier Piale Pasha (c. 1515-1578)
cd6b2c88-0a74-5d2f-8cba-5b3ea7174b9c.description: These tiles decorated the palace of the Ottoman Grand Vizier Piale Pasha, or possibly the mosque the Vizier commissioned. Both buildings were completed in 1573 and richly decorated with tile panels. The palace and the mosque were restored after an earthquake in 1890, and the tile panels were sold all over the world. At least nine identical tympanums are now in American and European museums.
cd6b2c88-0a74-5d2f-8cba-5b3ea7174b9c.holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art
cd6b2c88-0a74-5d2f-8cba-5b3ea7174b9c.materials: Frit ceramic with transparent enamel over white background with floral decoration in the colours darkblue, blue, turquoise and red (tomato red) with black contours

ce15a428-c117-5ec8-bdb2-e57a6da94a62.name: Villa Crespi
ce15a428-c117-5ec8-bdb2-e57a6da94a62.holder: Since the 1980s, Villa Crespi has been transformed in a 4-star hotel owned by the 'Villa Crespi-Ca.pri srl'
ce15a428-c117-5ec8-bdb2-e57a6da94a62.author: Ignazio Galella
ce15a428-c117-5ec8-bdb2-e57a6da94a62.history:
Cristoforo Benigno Crespi was a successful businessman active in the cotton industry. In 1879, he bought an estate near Lake d’Orta (Piedmont, Northern Italy), to build a vacation house in honour of his wife, Pia Travelli.  
Crespi had fallen in love with the architecture of Baghdad, where he went to buy cotton, and asked architect Angelo Colla to build for him a villa in Moorish style. Architect Enrico Combi designed the magnificent park.  
After it was inaugurated, the villa became a centre of high-society life: it hosted members of the Italian royal family and even the King of Spain. The Crespi organised theatre performances in the park and invited nobles, industrialists and bankers. At the end of the 1980s, Villa Crespi was transformed into a four-star hotel.
ce15a428-c117-5ec8-bdb2-e57a6da94a62.description2: An astonishing three-storey villa in Moorish style, near Lake d’Orta in Piedmont, Northern Italy. It features a 48-meter high minaret and has richly decorated interiors made with lavish marbles imported from several countries. Construction lasted 12 years. The estate includes a greenhouse, a wet dock, stables, a big fountain, an annex, and is surrounded by walls with valuable wrought iron gates.

d0602307-9a81-587d-b9b3-2b8e93c844eb.name: Al-Madina al-Munawwara Station
d0602307-9a81-587d-b9b3-2b8e93c844eb.holder: Saudi Commission for Tourism and Antiquities
d0602307-9a81-587d-b9b3-2b8e93c844eb.history:
The Hijaz railway was very important for the Islamic world where pilgrims could reach al-Hijaz safe and in short time comparing to what was before. The station was known in al-Madina as *istasyon*, a Turkish word meaning station.  
The station is located west of the Prophet 's Mohammed (PBU) Mosque and approximately 1 km a way, in the region now known Aanbariyah beside Anbariyah Mosque and Alanbariyah Gate, which was removed for the purpose of expanding the streets in the area.  
The first train arrived to al-Madina in 23rd of August 1908 and the official ceremony for the opening of the Station was held a week later.
d0602307-9a81-587d-b9b3-2b8e93c844eb.keywords: Hijaz; railway station; pilgrimage; hajj; pilgrimage route; caravan; sacred places; communication; innovation; architecture; Arabian Peninsula; Ottoman; Germany; Abdul Hamid; abd al-hamid
d0602307-9a81-587d-b9b3-2b8e93c844eb.architects: Mukhtar bey, the general manager of the line
d0602307-9a81-587d-b9b3-2b8e93c844eb.description2: The station is rectangular in shape with a length of about 700 meters and a width of about 150 meters, and is surrounded by a fence built of black basalt stone, and comprises a set of 11 buildings including the main one. All the station buildings and remaining trains and carriages were restored by the Saudi commission for Tourism and Antiquities and converted into an Islamic museum for the city of al-Madina.

d182a16f-df1f-5ece-848d-95d8514da95e.name: Glazed tile 'Butterflies'
d182a16f-df1f-5ece-848d-95d8514da95e.author: DGPC
d182a16f-df1f-5ece-848d-95d8514da95e.keywords: Azulejo; glazed tile; butterflies; Portuguese culture
d182a16f-df1f-5ece-848d-95d8514da95e.description2: The glazed tile or azulejo is a particularly expressive component of Portuguese art that is constantly being renovated. Between the end of the 19th century and beginning of the 20th century, it is strongly influenced by art nouveau, as is shown by this tile by Rafael Bordalo Pinheiro, made in one of Portugal’s main ceramic centres, the town of Caldas da Rainha.

d275ed47-c70f-5403-8c84-80462e835077.name: *The Savoy Hotel*
d275ed47-c70f-5403-8c84-80462e835077.keywords: Hotel; Landmarks of Egypt; Old Hotels; Tourism
d275ed47-c70f-5403-8c84-80462e835077.description2: The Savoy Hotel in downtown Cairo, known for its distinctive dome.

d320c5a3-16a0-5b02-8130-8a58ce2b34cb.name: Patriarchal College
d320c5a3-16a0-5b02-8130-8a58ce2b34cb.author: Hala Masri
d320c5a3-16a0-5b02-8130-8a58ce2b34cb.history:
Each confession in Lebanon worked on spreading its beliefs and principals. Therefore, religiously based educational institutions were built. In this case the catholic Greek Church inaugurated the Patriarchal College in 1865, and still exists nowadays.  
Many religious education institutions were built in Lebanon, a multi-confessional country, with the aim of spreading the beliefs and principles of the respective confession. This Patriarchal College was inaugurated by the Catholic Greek church in 1865 and is still in use today.
d320c5a3-16a0-5b02-8130-8a58ce2b34cb.description2:
During his reign Gregory founded both the Patriarchal College in Beirut in 1865 and the Patriarchal College in Damascus in 1875 and re-opened the Melkite seminary of 'Ayn Traz in 1866. A western kind of architecture with balconies and balustrades.  
Gregory II Youssef founded the Patriarchal College in Beirut in 1865 as well as the Patriarchal College in Damascus in 1875 and re-opened the Melkit seminary of 'Ayn Trez in 1866. The college was built in a Western style, as seen by the use of balconies and balustrades.

d33416a4-0a7d-53e7-981b-69aa3e40b575.name: *The Grand Bazaar Istanbul*
d33416a4-0a7d-53e7-981b-69aa3e40b575.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
d33416a4-0a7d-53e7-981b-69aa3e40b575.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
d33416a4-0a7d-53e7-981b-69aa3e40b575.description2: This painting provides a fascinating insight into the activities within the Grand Bazaar of Istanbul during the 19th century CE. First built in the 15th century, its importance had declined somewhat in the 19th century, as non-Muslim merchants increasingly established independent shops in the European quarters of Istanbul rather than staying in the ‘outdated’ bazaar. Nevertheless, in 1890, there were still well over 4000 shops in the Bazaar. This image provides much detail about the appearance of traditional merchants and shops. Men, including some soldiers in European-style uniforms, and women in colourful local dress can be seen milling about the bazaar, their costume revealing important details about their ethnicity, profession and social status.

d46c6076-f552-5c09-aeaa-96eb625e9090.name: Lady of Harissa
d46c6076-f552-5c09-aeaa-96eb625e9090.description: Harissa is a mountain village in Lebanon. Located 650 metres above sea level, it is home to an important pilgrimage site, the Our Lady of Lebanon statue, which attracts both pilgrims and tourists who want to enjoy the view of Jounieh bay. The statue, which is made of 15 tons of bronze painted white, shows the Virgin Mary with her arms out-stretched. The village itself is 20km north of Beirut, and accessible from the coastal city of Jounieh either by road or by cable car.
d46c6076-f552-5c09-aeaa-96eb625e9090.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
d46c6076-f552-5c09-aeaa-96eb625e9090.history: The Our Lady of Lebanon statue was built at the end of the 19th century and inaugurated in 1908. A small chapel occupies the base of the chapel, and a huge Maronite cathedral built of concrete and glass in a modern style stands beside the statue. Being a pilgrimage site, the statue has received many important visitors, such as Pope John Paul II in May 1997 and Pope Benedict XVI in September 2012.
d46c6076-f552-5c09-aeaa-96eb625e9090.keywords: Harissa; Virgin Mary; Pilgrims; Jounieh; Sanctuary; Statue

d51c4926-dec8-5d72-9ed4-34a107dddbd4.name: *Shipping at Constantinople*
d51c4926-dec8-5d72-9ed4-34a107dddbd4.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
d51c4926-dec8-5d72-9ed4-34a107dddbd4.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
d51c4926-dec8-5d72-9ed4-34a107dddbd4.description2: Istanbul’s geographic position between Europe and Asia and on the only sea route that connects the Black Sea with the Mediterranean gave Istanbul great strategic importance. The control of the Bosphorus, which connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Marmara, was repeatedly at stake in the 19th and early 20th centuries. This 1910 watercolour gives a wonderful impression of the bustling shipping and trading activities on the waters surrounding the city of Constantinople at the time. The view is taken from the Galata side of the city, looking across the Golden Horn towards its historic heart, dominated by imperial Suleymaniye mosque on the right and Bayezid tower in the centre. The Galata bridge, in its third incarnation as completed by the British firm G. Wells in 1875, can be seen connecting the two shores. Sailing boats like those seen here brought in wheat, spices and wood. The emergence of the steamship later in the century lead to enormous increase in the speed and volume of commodities shipped to Constantinople.

d616de70-37f8-5d6d-9c22-8c4a59417e94.name: Barbadinhos Steam pumping station
d616de70-37f8-5d6d-9c22-8c4a59417e94.holder: EPAL- Portuguese Society for Water Supply
d616de70-37f8-5d6d-9c22-8c4a59417e94.author: Bárbara Bruno
d616de70-37f8-5d6d-9c22-8c4a59417e94.history: Classified as CIP – Setting of Public Interest through Decree. º 1176/2010, DR, 2nd Series, no. 248 of 14/12/2010, the Station of Barbadinhos was designed to raise water from the Alviela river to the reservoir of Veronica and to the Cistern of Monte. Opened on 3 October 1880, the station considerably increased the volume of water supplied to the city of Lisbon. Its main equipment, consisting of four steam engines built in the workshops of E. W. Windsor of Rouen, ran until 1928.
d616de70-37f8-5d6d-9c22-8c4a59417e94.keywords: Lisbon water supply; Steam Machinery; Water Museum; Barbadinhos; industrial archaeology building
d616de70-37f8-5d6d-9c22-8c4a59417e94.architects: Windsor House & Fils and Workshops of CAL – Companhia das Águas de Lisboa (Water Company of Lisbon)
d616de70-37f8-5d6d-9c22-8c4a59417e94.description2: This Lisbon Water Museum is the urban memory symbol of innovation and improvements in public health issues. The Barbadinhos Steam Pumping Station opened on 3 October 1880. It was built to raise the water coming from the Alviela Canal to the Veronica and Cisterna do Monte reservoirs. It was used to increase the volume of the water supplied to the city of Lisbon. The main equipment consists of four steam machines that worked uninterruptedly until 1928. They were built in the workshops of “Constructeurs - Mecaniciens” E. W. Windsor & Fils, of Rouen, France, an English owned company. The machines, whose steam was produced by five boilers, are all of the same kind: vertical pistons with two cylinders each and steam liner – Woolf system – of variable expansion and condensation.

monument_contact.responsible_institution: EPAL – Empresa Portuguesa das Águas Livres, S.A.

d616de70-37f8-5d6d-9c22-8c4a59417e94.responsible_institution_org: EPAL – Empresa Portuguesa das Águas Livres, S.A.

d62a8aad-7189-5f2c-a39f-c9a6febe7aa4.name: *Ancient Istanbul Houses*
d62a8aad-7189-5f2c-a39f-c9a6febe7aa4.holder: Mimar Sinan Fine Arts University, Painting and Sculpture Museum
d62a8aad-7189-5f2c-a39f-c9a6febe7aa4.keywords: Painting; Hoca Ali Rıza; orientalist Turkish painters
d62a8aad-7189-5f2c-a39f-c9a6febe7aa4.description2: Hoca Ali Rıza is known as the first painter who used landscapes in Turkish painting. A study of the artist’s works also readily reveals architectural structures which have changed since his time. Such structures included mosques, fountains, dervish monasteries and lodges, tombs, *sebils* (public fountains installed by charities), ruins, cemeteries, bridges, stately homes new and old, towers, old houses and other subjects which architecturally and historically speaking might have been considered ordinary in his day, but which he pursued with a passion. Riza is completely realistic in his works and he specialized in depicting landscapes using light and shadow.

d6481ac4-6c4b-57b0-a7f3-e97d7469d47b.name: Central Hotel
d6481ac4-6c4b-57b0-a7f3-e97d7469d47b.history: The style of the building refers to contemporary architecture seen in European Mediterranean cities at the time.
d6481ac4-6c4b-57b0-a7f3-e97d7469d47b.keywords: French in Morocco; French in North Africa; protectorate; Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic influence; European influence; European architecture; hotel; travel; tourism; city; urban space; changes in urban spaces; colonial city; colonial building; urban planning; colonial architecture; colonial economy; city plan; Moroccan city
d6481ac4-6c4b-57b0-a7f3-e97d7469d47b.description2: A white Mediterranean-style building with three floors plus the ground floor, the facade has an open feel due to the blue-painted, geometrically ornamented wrought iron balconies, which echo designs seen in lacework and headbands. Located on Place Ahmad el Bidaoui (formerly Place Admiral Philibert), on the port side of the *Medina*, near the customs premises, the hotel played an important historical role in accommodating both tourists and officials.

d7b44516-bffd-5b76-8377-02433184be03.name: The Cairo Electric Railways and Heliopolis Oasis Company
d7b44516-bffd-5b76-8377-02433184be03.holder: Heliopolis Company for Housing and Development
d7b44516-bffd-5b76-8377-02433184be03.author: Ahmad al-Bindari
d7b44516-bffd-5b76-8377-02433184be03.history:
The HOC (Heliopolis Oases Company) was founded by decree on the 14th of February 1906. Its inception, however, came first in the 20th of May 1905 when the land was purchased and the railway concession was attained by both founders of Heliopolis: the Belgian Baron Edward Empain and Boghos Nubar Pasha.  
The company’s Neo-Mamluk premises were built in 1908, following the designs of Belgian architect Ernest Jaspar (1876–1940). Currently, the building houses the company that used to handle services in the suburbs of Heliopolis like water, gas, electricity, tramways, etc.
d7b44516-bffd-5b76-8377-02433184be03.keywords: The Cairo Electric Railways and Heliopolis Oases Company; Heliopolis Oasis Company (H.O.C.); Heliopolis Company for Housing and Development; Moorish Architecture; Neo-Mamluk Architecture; Islamic Architecture
d7b44516-bffd-5b76-8377-02433184be03.second_name: Heliopolis Oasis Company (H.O.C.); Heliopolis Company for Housing and Development (current name)
d7b44516-bffd-5b76-8377-02433184be03.description2: The first administrative premises of the Heliopolis Oases Company (HOC). The architecture of Heliopolis represents quite a unique and outstanding experiment with form architecture. The neighbourhood's buildings – mostly designed by French and Italian architects – followed the European styles of the time, employing the principal of Eclecticism. Features of Arab, Andalusian, Art Nouveau and Art Deco styles are characteristic of the district.

d7bf5b87-41a9-54ad-80be-78334ba1edff.name: 3 May 1919, demolishing the fortifications at Porte de Clignancourt
d7bf5b87-41a9-54ad-80be-78334ba1edff.description2: Between 1841 and 1844, Adolphe Thiers had a 33km long city wall built to protect Paris. These "fortif'" (fortifications), which were proved to be useless during the war in 1870, soon became inhabited by the poor. It was an area made up of shacks, and soon became a lawless zone. The demolition of the "fortif" began in Clignancourt in 1919, in order to make way for new urbanisation projects and disperse the inhabitants. In this photograph, we can see the neighbourhood children contributing to the works.

d91bd95e-d043-5ebb-9f83-4ff6245ed95a.name: House of the Robev family
d91bd95e-d043-5ebb-9f83-4ff6245ed95a.author: Nada Andonovska
d91bd95e-d043-5ebb-9f83-4ff6245ed95a.history: The construction of the first house of the Robev family was finished on the 15 April 1827 as witnessed by the inscription in Greek on the marbled flagstone. It was rebuilt in 1863–1864. Construction foreman Todor Petkov built the house from scratch. Konstantin Robev lived in the left part of the house and his brother Atanas Robev in the right one. The two families lived in the newly built house until 1900 when they moved to Bitola and used the house as a summer residence. At present this building houses the exhibition galleries of the Institute for Protection of Culture Monuments and Museum of Ohrid.
d91bd95e-d043-5ebb-9f83-4ff6245ed95a.description2: The house of the Robev family is one of the highlights of traditional urban architecture in Macedonia. It represents the best of the distinctive style of Ohrid architecture, as well as exquisite layout and interior decor. The house was listed as protected architectural heritage after the First World War. It is a three-storied house having been divided vertically into two parts (left and right), thus belonging to the type of brothers' house traditionally built in Macedonia in the 19th and 20th centuries. The distinctive features of this structure are protruding decks expanding the usable surface on the second and third stories. The most outstanding elements decorating the interior of the house are niches in the walls, as well as wood-carved ornaments applied in the rooms and on the ceilings.

da0ac07d-2149-50b6-a034-3d3ec0987ead.name: *Al-Maryamiyya (St. Mary’s Church), Damascus*
da0ac07d-2149-50b6-a034-3d3ec0987ead.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
da0ac07d-2149-50b6-a034-3d3ec0987ead.author: Stefan Weber
da0ac07d-2149-50b6-a034-3d3ec0987ead.second_name: Main church aisle towards the iconostasis
da0ac07d-2149-50b6-a034-3d3ec0987ead.description2: This church was a late 4th century foundation, which was, after its destruction in 1860, rebuilt in red brick with the financial support from Russia. Today the Maryamiyya Church, one of the oldest Greek-Orthodox churches in Damascus, is still very  popular and regularly used by the Christian community there.

db057e21-fbd4-560f-92fe-dac033689842.name: Dar al-Batha (Batha Museum)
db057e21-fbd4-560f-92fe-dac033689842.history: Although the foundations for the Palace of Dar el-Batha were laid during the reign of Mulay al-Hasan I, it was completed during the reign of Mulay ‘Abd al-‘Aziz in 1897. The palace was used for private meetings, receptions and sometimes as a summer residence. The Museum of Arts and Traditions of Fez and its region took over the palace in 1915 and, although the building was altered at this time, the outline of its plan has remained intact.
db057e21-fbd4-560f-92fe-dac033689842.keywords: Palace; royal palace; public space; private space; garden; Islamic garden; gardens and architecture; Islamic city; Moroccan city; traditional city; urban space; urban planning; plan; house; traditional house; North African house; Moroccan architects; Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic influence
db057e21-fbd4-560f-92fe-dac033689842.second_name: Pavillion of the Royal Palace in Fez
db057e21-fbd4-560f-92fe-dac033689842.description2: Dar al-Batha is the site of a large palace with two wings (east and west) and separate dwellings located at either side of a rectangular Andalusian-type garden (*riyadh*), which also surrounds the entire main palace. Within the palace are some large rectangular rooms that lead on to porches, at the corners of which are doors opening to outbuildings and annexes (*Douira*, sheds or *khzine*, etc.), and leading to the basement (now the Palace Museum) from which one can access the nearby Batha Square. Two side galleries (north and south) connect the two wings with the main house.

db149753-6678-5bb1-939e-d9e0339d08a2.name: Yıldız Palace Small State Kiosk
db149753-6678-5bb1-939e-d9e0339d08a2.notice: This is an unedited Database entry and may contain errors and inconsistencies in spelling. We are working to raise the funds required to complete the editing; should you wish to contribute please visit our [Support page](https://www.museumwnf.org/atrium_support.php).
db149753-6678-5bb1-939e-d9e0339d08a2.history:
Yildiz Palace, which is the last architectural example of Turkish Ottoman palace, is located on the Yildiz hill in the district of Besiktas. Sultan Ahmed I was the first to build a pavilion, over this land registered at the time to the Private treasury of the Ottoman Sultan as a hunting place sultans beginning during the reign of Suleiman the Magnificent (1520-1566).  
The main construction in the palace started in the period of Sultan Abdulhamid II (1876-1909) and it was called Saray-i Humayun (Central palace). During this period the palace comprised of buildings for private use of the sultan as well as buildings, allocated for the officials, repair shops and carpentry like repairing shop, carpenter’s shop and the buildings of culture and art such as theatre, museum and library. The Palace begun to serve as a museum under the name of “Directorate of the Museum of Yildiz Palace since 1993.
db149753-6678-5bb1-939e-d9e0339d08a2.description2: Small State Kiosk was built in 1901 as the studying and resting kiosks upon the order of Sultan Abdulhamid II. The Sultan was holding official meetings here and it was used for the same purpose by the subsequent sultans. The two storied building has also a garret known as Winter Garden. The kiosk is famous for its ceiling decorations, the handrails decorated with flower branches in the form of elegant Art Nouveau and leaded windows bearing Bonet s signature. Sultan Abdulhamid II was informed about his dethronement in this kiosk. After his residence in Dolmabance Palace, Sultan Vahidettin settled in Yildiz Palace and made his interviews in this kiosk in the armistice period. Mustafa Kemal Ataturk also met Sultan Vahidettin for the last time on May 15th, 1919, in one of the room of this kiosk , before heading to Samsun with the title of 3rd Army Inspector.

dc296dc9-ccb7-508b-bd42-c197d02e0db4.name: Çakırağa Mansion
dc296dc9-ccb7-508b-bd42-c197d02e0db4.keywords: Birgi; Ödemiş; house; mansion; sofa (hayat); decoration; wall painting; woodwork; ceiling decoration; vegetal decoration; geometric decoration; landscape; architectural compositions; still life; trompe l’oeil
dc296dc9-ccb7-508b-bd42-c197d02e0db4.description2: This private mansion is one of the most authentic surviving examples of an Anatolian Turkish house with its layout and painted and woodwork decoration. This monumental mansion is three-storeyed and has a courtyard-garden. The ground floor, which is paved with stone plaques, is given over to service rooms. The living quarters on the upper two floors have an outer *sofa*. Among the wall paintings on the exterior and interior walls of the structure are noteworthy panoramas of Istanbul and Izmir. The wooden ceilings and cupboards have remarkable decoration. The structure has been open to public as a museum since 1995.

dc5bc0bc-3826-5d4a-a791-7c22130aca80.name: *Pool of Siloam*
dc5bc0bc-3826-5d4a-a791-7c22130aca80.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)
dc5bc0bc-3826-5d4a-a791-7c22130aca80.archival: Jewry afterwards Valentine, Laura, *Palestine Past and Present. Pictorial and descriptive ... Illustrated, etc*, London: F. Warne & Co, 1893, p. 127
dc5bc0bc-3826-5d4a-a791-7c22130aca80.keywords: Pilgrimage; pilgrims; Christian pilgrimage; Jewish pilgrimage; Palestine; Holy Land; Jerusalem; sacred places; travel; travel book; Ottoman Palestine; local Jewish community; Biblical places; Biblical archaology
dc5bc0bc-3826-5d4a-a791-7c22130aca80.description2: The description of the Pool of Siloam is included in the chapter about Jerusalem in the book *Palestine Past and Present* by Laura Jewry Valentine. The book provides a historical and archaeological description of the place, reporting the story of its discovery and identification with the site that is referred to in Jewish and Christian tradition.

dc607c77-31f1-570e-8446-1bb4e69fad90.name: Courtyard house
dc607c77-31f1-570e-8446-1bb4e69fad90.description: The central courtyard would include a water fountain, occasionally a small square garden, and would be separated from the street by high surrounding walls. This particular courtyard is accessed by a relatively low arched door. The main building (*al dakhil dar*, meaning indoor building) is north facing, whereas the smaller outdoor buildings (*al-barrani*) such as the kitchen, pantry and toilet, are generally located on the east side. The living quarters included a central living room and two square side rooms. The central living room is an enclosed shared space, keeping the inhabitants dry on rainy days and cool on hot summer days.
dc607c77-31f1-570e-8446-1bb4e69fad90.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Julien El Khoury
dc607c77-31f1-570e-8446-1bb4e69fad90.history:
Older courtyard houses built with clay walls resting on wooden beams began to be replaced by concrete slabs with supporting walls made of *ramleh*, as we can see from this example. In other areas, such as Ashrafiyyeh, the old style was replaced with alternating sandstone and limestone-marl walls, a style known as *ablaq*.  
The *dar* is built on a principle of scalability: rooms were added as the number of inhabitants expanded and thus the building was able grow without any changes to its internal logic. This kind of house became popular in the 1850s, and generally belonged to the city's aristocracy. It was specifically designed to be able to host the same family in the same building across many generations.

e04ca700-4cef-584a-b2aa-bf9feabea8a0.name: Université Saint-Joseph (USJ)
e04ca700-4cef-584a-b2aa-bf9feabea8a0.description: Jesuits were very active in Lebanon in the 19th century. They founded a small school in Beirut in 1839, and then a larger school in Ghazir (Keserwan) in 1855, which would be moved to Beirut in 1875 and become the Saint Joseph University. It was granted the title of "university" by the local authorities, which allowed it to issue academic degrees, mainly doctoral degrees in philosophy and theology. Various faculties were founded soon after, such as the Institute of Medicine in 1883, which would become the Faculty of Medicine in 1888, and the Faculty of Medicine and Pharmacy a year later. A Maternity clinic opened in 1896, followed by the Oriental College in 1902 and the School for French Law in 1913, which became the Faculty of Law in 1946. The French School in Engineering was also founded in 1913, and became the Higher Institute for Engineering in 1948.
e04ca700-4cef-584a-b2aa-bf9feabea8a0.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
e04ca700-4cef-584a-b2aa-bf9feabea8a0.history: The Université Saint-Joseph (USJ) in Beirut evolved from a seminary founded by Jesuits in Ghazir in 1843. The Collège in Ghazir, intended to train the local Maronite clergy, relocated to Beirut in 1875 where it took the name of Saint Joseph University.
e04ca700-4cef-584a-b2aa-bf9feabea8a0.keywords: University; St Joseph; Beirut; Jesuits; Christians; Education

e1be7517-b6b1-576b-8acd-653f24c29ba9.name: *Hijaz Railway Station, Damascus*
e1be7517-b6b1-576b-8acd-653f24c29ba9.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
e1be7517-b6b1-576b-8acd-653f24c29ba9.author: Stefan Weber
e1be7517-b6b1-576b-8acd-653f24c29ba9.second_name: Main Station of the Hijaz railway leading from Damascus to Medina
e1be7517-b6b1-576b-8acd-653f24c29ba9.description2: The Hijaz station was originally built in 1903 to provide faster transportation for Pilgrims to Medina. So the today closed-down railway station used to be an essential transport and communication link. Furthermore it was built to integrate aloof provinces better into the Ottoman state and hence establish a closer political and economic connection. The new building completed in 1917 also embodies a desire for innovation in terms of design: its architecture is a mix between traditional local Ottoman elements and monumentalizing features of historicism.

e24c667e-3e74-52ad-9357-51224ea2c3d0.name: A letter from the Hashemite court
e24c667e-3e74-52ad-9357-51224ea2c3d0.description: A letter from the Hashemite court signed by al-Hussein bin 'Ali, the king of Arab countries and Sharif of Mecca. The letter was sent to the princes Faisal and al-Aziz al-Jarba, from Umm al-Qura (Mecca) in Rajab, 18th, AH 1336 / AD 1917 asking them to take care of Jacobean Armenian confession and to help them and to protect them as they protect themselves, their fortune and their sons. It says also to facilitate what they need either in their stay or travel, because they are free non-Muslims enjoying Muslim protection. Those are people who prophet Muhammad makes his will to take care of, and the one who doesn’t do so will be his (Muhammad's) adversary till Judgment Day. King Hussein says: this is one of the most important orders we ask you to do. He ends his letter by praying to God to grant the Emirs to do what he asks them.
e24c667e-3e74-52ad-9357-51224ea2c3d0.author: Aida Naghawi
e24c667e-3e74-52ad-9357-51224ea2c3d0.keywords: Hussein bin Ali; king of Arab countries; Sharif of Mecca; Jacobean Armenian; free non-Muslims; Muslim protection;

e2b48175-dfa4-5317-9f12-0d280735f099.name: Drawing of the railway bridge between the mainland and Venice
e2b48175-dfa4-5317-9f12-0d280735f099.description2: This panoramic view shows the railway link between Venice and the mainland. In 1837 a company was founded to organize the building of the railway in the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia. Construction started in 1840 and the railway reached the Venetian station of Santa Lucia in 1846.

e33b8e98-0a42-5720-b63c-c7e462cb0c9c.name: School of the Voz do Operário (Voice of the Worker) society, external view
e33b8e98-0a42-5720-b63c-c7e462cb0c9c.description: Lisbon: School Voz do Operário created by tobacco working class association in 1879. This label – Voz do Operário – was used also to mention the working newspaper, the working welfare cares and the support to the working class funerals.
e33b8e98-0a42-5720-b63c-c7e462cb0c9c.holder: Photography Archive, Lisbon City Council, CML
e33b8e98-0a42-5720-b63c-c7e462cb0c9c.author: Cristina Correia
e33b8e98-0a42-5720-b63c-c7e462cb0c9c.keywords: Reform; social changes; Politcal Context; Cities urban spaces; trade union; worker; rights of workers; welfare

e4e13104-3af0-5b6e-9e16-b30a037f184b.name: *Wilaya* (district), Casablanca
e4e13104-3af0-5b6e-9e16-b30a037f184b.history: The first plan was drawn in 1914, but construction according to the designs of French architect Marius Boyer was not completed until 1936. Formerly a prestigious hotel and one of grandest buildings on Place Mohammed V, it is still well preserved.
e4e13104-3af0-5b6e-9e16-b30a037f184b.keywords: Moorish style; art deco; Art Nouveau; Vienna; French in Morocco; French in North Africa; French architects in North Africa; protectorate; Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic influence; Islamic city; European influence; European architecture; hotel; travel; tourism; city; urban space; changes in urban spaces; colonial city; colonial building; colonial architecture; urban planning
e4e13104-3af0-5b6e-9e16-b30a037f184b.description2: This now-administrative building, formerly a hotel, is of notable design and colossal dimensions. The entrance has three large doorways with extensive copper surrounds, two large blank windows, and four small windows. It is highlighted by a gallery supported by large hexagonal stone pillars. The window openings – of different sizes and in different styles – pointed horseshoe and curved arches, have sandstone surrounds. The first-floor gallery has rich, predominantly green *zellige* decoration. The building is topped by a square clock tower with a timepiece on all four sides.

e6f7eabb-fc4e-5c98-b6ca-f2544ae496d9.name: Model in plaster
e6f7eabb-fc4e-5c98-b6ca-f2544ae496d9.description: Following on the European fascination for the oriental world and for the famous Nasrid Palaces of the Alhambra (Granada, Spain), a lot of reproductions of its remarkable architectures and decorations were made and spread. José Contreras was commended as restorer and decorator and his son, Rafael (1824–1890), was the leading pioneer of this trend in 1847. His work was continued by the grandson and by a huge number of plaster-cast workshops in Granada, and very likely, in other cities. His plasterworks were very successful in the International Exhibitions and were kept in private collections and museums like South Kensington (London). This polychrome plaster cast res a window in the Mexnar Palace of Granada (Spain).
e6f7eabb-fc4e-5c98-b6ca-f2544ae496d9.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes, Cristina Giménez

e714183d-faa1-5c38-bf56-e05a8f41f61e.name: Bab el-Bhar - Porte de France
e714183d-faa1-5c38-bf56-e05a8f41f61e.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
e714183d-faa1-5c38-bf56-e05a8f41f61e.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
e714183d-faa1-5c38-bf56-e05a8f41f61e.archival: Tunis au XIXe Siècle: Aquarelles et Textes de Charles Lallemand, Apollonia, 2001.
e714183d-faa1-5c38-bf56-e05a8f41f61e.keywords: Porte de France; Tunis medina; European quarter
e714183d-faa1-5c38-bf56-e05a8f41f61e.description2: This copy of a beautiful watercolour from Charles Lallemand's book *Tunis et ses Environs* shows the Porte de la Mer, or the Porte de France, around which both European settlers and Tunisian residents are gathered. Its location was strategic, as it led to both the Tunis medina and the European quarter.

e71e341d-eb52-561e-8abf-141b52235da5.name: St. Andrew's Church
e71e341d-eb52-561e-8abf-141b52235da5.history: The land for the church was donated by Sultan Mulay ‘Abd ‘Aziz in 1880 to serve the British Christian community in Tangier. Soon it was found that the building was not sufficient for the growing number of worshippers, so a new one was built in 1894, which became the church of St. Andrew. It was consecrated in 1905.
e71e341d-eb52-561e-8abf-141b52235da5.keywords: Religious building; tolerance; plaster; painted wood; marble; geometric decoration; vegetal decoration; epigraphic decoration; British in Morocco; Morocaan architects; craftsmen; craftsmanship; Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic influence; Islamic architecture in Morocco; public space
e71e341d-eb52-561e-8abf-141b52235da5.description2: Built on a plot of land donated by Sultan Mulay ‘Abd ‘Aziz, both church and grounds served British Christian residents. In the grounds alongside the church, there is a cemetery that contains the graves of some well-known English personalities such as *The Times* correspondent Walter Harris. In both style and decoration, the building’s Arab-Islamic inspiration is testimony to the Moroccan workers and craftsmen that constructed it. The belfry, built in the style of Moroccan mosque minarets, is square, its base decorated with mosaic and high-relief stucco geometric decoration. Doors and windows are a mixture of round-horseshoe and pointed-horseshoe arches. The canopy over the main entrance is of wood, decorated with brackets. Inside, twin marble columns separate the nave; the choir is accessed through a horseshoe arch that is surrounded with floral decoration, again in high-relief stucco. The arch-surround is framed by text from the gospel in *kufic* script. The ceiling is of painted woodwork and the roof is covered with green tiles. Located behind the altar, the niche is decorated with plaster latticework that holds the motto of Nasrid Granada “There is no conqueror but God”.

e77f7585-833b-5120-a08a-4e03b131f833.name: *Interior of the Great Temple at Baalbec*
e77f7585-833b-5120-a08a-4e03b131f833.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
e77f7585-833b-5120-a08a-4e03b131f833.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
e77f7585-833b-5120-a08a-4e03b131f833.artist: Drawn by William Henry Bartlett; engraved by Ebenezar Challis
e77f7585-833b-5120-a08a-4e03b131f833.description2: This view into the interior of the Temple of Bacchus at Baalbek, Lebanon originally formed appeared in 'Syria, The Holy Land, Asia Minor, &c', illustrated views printed in 3 series over 2 volumes (37 plates, 37 plates, and 48 plates for each series respectively) including maps and title pages. The publication resulted from the 1836-1838 collaboration between the painter William Henry Bartlett, the engraver Ebenezer Challis and the Publishers Fisher, Son and Co. The architectural and artistic details they recorded subsequently inspired European Neoclassical architects and artists such as Robert Adam, who based one of the ceilings at Osterley House on the ceiling of the Temple of Bacchus and the portico of St George's, Bloomsbury on its portico. Since the 1860s, many tourists visited the site, including, in 1898, the German emperor Wilhelm II. Struck by the magnificence of the ruins, he dispatched a German archaeological team, whose subsequent work resulted in a meticulous, illustrated publication that further popularised the site.

e8b27287-7930-5858-8acb-830809b29cd2.name: Saint George Church (Mar Gerges)
e8b27287-7930-5858-8acb-830809b29cd2.description: Located south-west of the 'Judge's well', this Greek Orthodox church was built by Batroun's chief mason, Tanios Deebo, with Batroun sandstone. The main gate, on the southern side, however, was built in limestone from Tum. The church consists of two vaults: one is a cupola, the tallest cupola in Lebanon, and the other is in the form of a cross and overlooks the altar. This church is notable for the two women's niches located under the dome on the north and south sides.
e8b27287-7930-5858-8acb-830809b29cd2.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
e8b27287-7930-5858-8acb-830809b29cd2.history: This Greek Orthodox church was built in a Byzantine style, with a remarkable dome that was completed in August 1867.
e8b27287-7930-5858-8acb-830809b29cd2.keywords: Church; Religion; Batroun; Sandstone; Cupola; Cross; Dome

e93e2356-ce89-5c16-b735-40f476c4b07d.name: Gustave Eiffel. The Eiffel Tower in 1889.
e93e2356-ce89-5c16-b735-40f476c4b07d.description2: Today, the Eiffel Tower is one of the great symbols of Paris and of France. This metal structure, a huge technological achievement in and of itself, was constructed by Gustave Eiffel (1823–1923) for the Exposition Universelle (world fair) of 1889, which celebrated the centenary of the French revolution. Many of his contemporaries, such as Guy de Maupassant, considered the structure hideous and called for its demolition. This drawing recalls the tower's function as a symbol of the vitality of French industry, highlighting its exceptional size and its proximity to the great Palais de l'Industrie, which housed the Dôme Central, the first building to use electricity on a large-scale.

e94849dd-ffd1-5aaf-9003-7370d13bf18e.name: Traditional Lebanese house
e94849dd-ffd1-5aaf-9003-7370d13bf18e.description: Houses in the nineteenth century were generally rather modest: roofs were supported by wooden beams, and whilst a handful of houses had stone stairs indoors as well as outdoors, most had only wooden stairs indoors.
e94849dd-ffd1-5aaf-9003-7370d13bf18e.author: Jeff El-Msanne
e94849dd-ffd1-5aaf-9003-7370d13bf18e.history: Mount Lebanon was well known, during the 19th century, for its houses with high ceilings and red roof tiles. The windows were generally made of wood and tinted glass, with the first floor opening out onto a balcony with tall windows for lighting and ventilation. This architectural style has clear signs of European influence.

e9dc3805-7eb0-5025-b948-d69dd0ddfe00.name: *The Citadel of Cairo, the Residence of the Pasha*
e9dc3805-7eb0-5025-b948-d69dd0ddfe00.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
e9dc3805-7eb0-5025-b948-d69dd0ddfe00.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
e9dc3805-7eb0-5025-b948-d69dd0ddfe00.description2: The citadel of Cairo, here captured by the Scottish artist David Roberts in the 1830s, was undergoing major changes under Muhammad Ali Pasha (1769-1849). Having overcome the Mamluks of Egypt in 1805, Muhammad Ali erased all traces of their rule, including remaining palace and administrative structures. He rebuilt most of the walls, erected four new palaces - his own royal residence in the northern enclosure, a courthouse, an expansive terrace and state-of-the-art accomodation for his army. At the heart of the citadel complex, Mohammad Pasha ordered a memorial mosque for his son Tusun in the Ottoman style. Building work on the mosque lasted from 1828 to 1848. Roberts incorporates the new structures existing in his time, like the palace on the right, cresting the hill - the ongoing building works on the mosque are concealed by the Mamluk structure in the foreground on the right.
e9dc3805-7eb0-5025-b948-d69dd0ddfe00.artist_birthplace: David Roberts: Edinburgh, Scotland; Louis Hague: Tournai, Belgium
e9dc3805-7eb0-5025-b948-d69dd0ddfe00.artist_deathplace: David Roberts: London; Louis Hague: London

ea530416-e3b0-5749-9237-eed6b02b7d4b.name: Ancient Egyptian Agricultural museum main entrance pathway and garden
ea530416-e3b0-5749-9237-eed6b02b7d4b.author: Ibrahim Abdel Aziz
ea530416-e3b0-5749-9237-eed6b02b7d4b.history:
King Fu\`ad I chose the palace of Fatma Ismail, the daughter of Khedive Ismail, ‎to host the displays of the Agricultural Museum. The ‎palace was chosen due to its location near the Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture in the ‎neighborhood of Dokki in Cairo.  
The museum, which was first called "The Agricultural Museum of King Fu\`ad I", was officially opened for the public on the 16th of January 1938 in a big ceremony that the king himself attended.
ea530416-e3b0-5749-9237-eed6b02b7d4b.keywords: Agricultural museum; Dokki, Agriculture Palace; Khedive Ismail; King Fu`ad I; Princess Fatma; Khedivial palaces; Khedivial Egypt; Ancient Agriculture; Pharaonic Agriculture
ea530416-e3b0-5749-9237-eed6b02b7d4b.description2: The museum of Ancient Egyptian Agriculture is the most interesting section of the Agricultural Museum and it contains the most valuable displays. Tourist groups must receive permission beforehand in order to visit this museum. It represents the first section of the development of agriculture in Egypt ‎and it illustrates the ‎history of Egyptian agriculture from the prehistoric period till the late Pharaonic ‎period. ‎The first floor of the museum of Ancient Egyptian Agriculture hosts all sorts of ‎displays that illustrate how the ancient Egyptians cultivated their lands. The displays ‎include ancient tools and equipment that were used in the days of the Pharaohs and descriptions of ‎how the ancient Egyptians created these tools.

eb84b6d8-fe2b-592c-9960-26f03ef21c4d.name: House
eb84b6d8-fe2b-592c-9960-26f03ef21c4d.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Prof. Marula Nikoloska, Ph.D. (consultant)
eb84b6d8-fe2b-592c-9960-26f03ef21c4d.history: This traditional house in Macedonia shows the influence of Levantine architecture, which was largely enhanced by the skills and knowledge of local masters bringing about outstanding architectural achievements. The town of Krushevo emerged in a relatively short period of about half a century in the late 1700s and early 1800s. Vlachs from Moscopole and minor places around it migrated to this area, bringing with them their construction and dwelling culture and tradition. Miyaks from the Reka area also moved here enriching the architecture with their great construction and architectural decoration skills.
eb84b6d8-fe2b-592c-9960-26f03ef21c4d.description2: The distinctive layout and interior organization of Krushevo houses arose from the need for adjustment to the steep terrain and severe climate. This house is a two-storied structure with a basement. As in most houses in Krushevo, levelling of structures has been done by construction of a basement embedded in the steep terrain. The basement was built of stone and the upper stories of adobe are coated with plaster. The usable space of the second storey has been expanded by protruded decks. The abundant decorative treatment of the front façade includes symmetrically laid windows flanking the balcony door on the second storey. The impression is enhanced by the peaked roof-edge and semi-round decorations above the balcony door and central windows.

ece4e33c-7204-5b42-8e58-18b1ae8b4d17.name: *Ruins of Troy: general excavation plan by Mr Schliemann*
ece4e33c-7204-5b42-8e58-18b1ae8b4d17.keywords: Greek antiquities; archaeological excavations; Schliemann; Turkey; plans
ece4e33c-7204-5b42-8e58-18b1ae8b4d17.description2: Heinrich Schliemann (1822–1890) was a German businessman who discovered his passion for archaeology whilst travelling. In 1870 he decided to direct an archaeological campaign in Turkey where he discovered the ruins of Troy. Various scandals (stolen objects, scientific errors) quickly destroyed his reputation, and today he is credited only with having created sites which led to important advances in the field. However, this plan of Troy is evidence for Schliemann's efforts to direct the excavations in a rigorous scientific manner.

edd18c27-fe22-5339-967d-92f28407d76f.name: House
edd18c27-fe22-5339-967d-92f28407d76f.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Prof. Petar Namichev (consultant)
