edd18c27-fe22-5339-967d-92f28407d76f.history: As most of the architectural heritage in Macedonia, dwelling architecture of the Maleshevo Region developed a mode of construction combining locally available building materials: stone, wood and earth. In the Berovo area in particular, the proximity of forests led to wide use of wood, not only as material for composing the structural elements but also for building walls.
edd18c27-fe22-5339-967d-92f28407d76f.description2: This house, built with a wooden framework, stone and earth, represents the specific traditional style of Macedonian dwelling architecture that developed under both Western and Oriental influences. It is a two-storey house constructed in the traditional style of the Maleshevo Region in the east of Macedonia. The ground floor consists of massive stone walls. The upper storey was built of horizontally laid laths and coated with mortar. The usable surface of the upper storey has been expanded by protrusions on the two sides of the house, supported by wooden poles and laths.

ee1f0807-ca9d-507c-adf4-27f446a10f42.name: Statue of Athlete – Ephesos
ee1f0807-ca9d-507c-adf4-27f446a10f42.description: After competitions in the *palestra* (sports arena), it was customary for the athletes to clean the sand from their oiled bodies with a strigil, or scraping iron. The Ephesian athlete seen here has already finished this task and – with his hair still soaking in sweat – is cleaning the strigil itself. This statue cannot be attributed to any Greek artist with certainty, yet Roman reproductions in marble and depictions on pottery reliefs and engraved stones speak to a high degree of familiarity with the original.
ee1f0807-ca9d-507c-adf4-27f446a10f42.holder: Kunsthistorisches Museum, Collection of Greek and Roman Antiquities
ee1f0807-ca9d-507c-adf4-27f446a10f42.dates: 2nd century AD (copy after a Greek original from the last quarter of the 4th century BC); found in 1895
ee1f0807-ca9d-507c-adf4-27f446a10f42.keywords: Ephesos; Abdul Hamid II; Emperor Franz Joseph

eefb1961-57d7-5239-9988-b5ce36ab258e.name: Triple-arched house
eefb1961-57d7-5239-9988-b5ce36ab258e.description: The layout of this house is composed of various rooms, symmetrically arranged around three sides of a large, north-facing central room called a *dar*. Three large arched windows, in a neo-gothic style, open onto a narrow balcony. The three sides of rooms do not communicate with each other, and thus the *dar* is both a communal living space and the physical centre of the home.
eefb1961-57d7-5239-9988-b5ce36ab258e.author: Jeff El-Msanne, David Andos
eefb1961-57d7-5239-9988-b5ce36ab258e.history: This kind of house started appearing around Beirut in the 1860s. It is often read as being representative of "Ottoman modernity" during the Tanzimat period, and its design and construction was outlined in/limited by the law. Indeed, this new architectural style was based on a new conception of the domestic space: domestic activities have been absorbed into the living space, and outdoor spaces are less prevalent. Balconies, backyards, courtyards and gardens, for example, no longer play an important role in the design of these homes.

ef89ce14-252d-5bb0-8014-da9c14164139.name: *Egypt. Construction of the Suez canal: the construction workers*
ef89ce14-252d-5bb0-8014-da9c14164139.keywords: Suez canal; Egypt; Ferdinand de Lesseps
ef89ce14-252d-5bb0-8014-da9c14164139.second_name: Taken from *Canal Maritime de Suez: Photographies D'apres Nature par Justin Kozlowski*
ef89ce14-252d-5bb0-8014-da9c14164139.description2: Photographers such as Justin Kozlowski photographed the excavation works throughout the construction of the Suez Canal. In contrast to the usual photos of Egypt which were taken for tourists, photographs such as this were taken for documentary purposes: it allowed the Suez Canal Company to see the progress and cost of the works.

f1166cb3-b783-5cbf-98fd-cd4d924c210b.name: Main entrance of the Hotel Excelsior at the Lido in Venice
f1166cb3-b783-5cbf-98fd-cd4d924c210b.holder: Archivio Progetti – Università Iuav di Venezia
f1166cb3-b783-5cbf-98fd-cd4d924c210b.author: Riccardo Domenichini
f1166cb3-b783-5cbf-98fd-cd4d924c210b.description2: The drawing shows the main entrance of the Hotel Excelsior on the beach of the Lido sandbar which separates the Venice lagoon from the sea. Two small towers crowned by domes with decorations stand aside the portal. Particularly interesting is the use of arches in Moorish style, for the main portal and for the loggias in the side wings.

f16ca057-a0e1-511d-9754-d9f37c51ca07.name: Kız Kulesi, Galata and Fındıklı Residential Areas
f16ca057-a0e1-511d-9754-d9f37c51ca07.keywords: Photograph; Old İstanbul Photograph; İstanbul; Pascal Sebah
f16ca057-a0e1-511d-9754-d9f37c51ca07.description2: Pascal Sébah (1823-1886) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. In 1857 he opened his first photography studio, *El Chark Societe Photographic*, in Istanbul and by 1873 was successful enough to open another studio in Cairo. In 1860 he moved to another studio next to the Russian Embassy in order to work with A. Laroche, who worked in Paris. He continued to work with Laroche until 1873.

f2f8e110-2548-568d-9481-67689f396cdc.name: Al-Zubarah
f2f8e110-2548-568d-9481-67689f396cdc.dates: 5th millennium BC; 18th century settlement; abandoned probably at the beginning of the 20th century
f2f8e110-2548-568d-9481-67689f396cdc.history:
Earliest human occupation near the site of al-Zubarah may date back as early as the Late Neolithic period (5th millennium BC). The ceramic assemblage recovered from al-Zubarah site itself is pointing to a possible Abbasid (8th – 9th century AD) occupation, prior to a Late Islamic village existing during the final period of the reign of Safavids in the upper Gulf region (18th century).  
According to the current knowledge, the major development of the town took place after the arrival of the Utub-tribe in northern Qatar. Al-Zubarah flowered during the 2nd half of the 18th century AD and played an important political role until it was totally destroyed after a major attack of Omani led forces in 1811.  
In a second phase of occupation after this event the city was considerably smaller. It never obtained the same importance than the 18th century settlement and by the beginning of the 20th century, the village was probably left abandoned.
f2f8e110-2548-568d-9481-67689f396cdc.description2:
The ruins of Al Zubarah are a traditionally well-known tourist destination in Qatar.  
Recognized as an archaeological site as early as in the 1950es by a Danish led team of archaeologists, the first systematic archaeological excavations were conducted in 1983. Under the direction of the National Museum of Qatar, the Qatari team uncovered several structures in the northern part of the ruins. Later on, the attention was turned to what was identified as the suq area and the inner quarters.

f30ed628-c2e1-59e3-9002-64e3343526ab.name: Karpino Monastery
f30ed628-c2e1-59e3-9002-64e3343526ab.author: Nada Andonovska
f30ed628-c2e1-59e3-9002-64e3343526ab.history: According to the legends, the monastery was originally built in the 14th century, having been set on fire and reconstructed many times. The present-day edifice of the Karpino Monastery dates from 1892, when it was restored to preserve some portions of the structure and frescoes dating from the 16th and 17th centuries. Throughout the Middle Ages, the monastery was a sanctuary for many Macedonian monks who acquired their education to become priests and serve God and the Church. Extensive literary activities were developed there by monks who used to prescribe various liturgical books, manuscripts and other patristic literature. In the late 19th century, monks from the Karpino Monastery formed a public school for teaching children from neighbouring villages.
f30ed628-c2e1-59e3-9002-64e3343526ab.description2: The Karpino Monastery was the cultural and literary centre of the Kumanovo region throughout the Middle Ages. The Church within the Karpino Monastery is dedicated to the Presentation of the Virgin in the Temple. It was built of crafted stone in the form of a single-nave basilica with an apse forming a triconch. Parts of the 16th and 17th-century edifice and wall paintings have been preserved during its reconstruction in 1892, including the frescoes depicting the Virgin and Child, as well as the effigies of St. Theodore Tyron and St. Theodore Stratylates. The exquisite early 17th-century wooden iconostasis has been preserved in the Monastery Church including seven valuable original icons which were painted by Nikola Zoograf and his students.

f3942bb8-28a9-5994-bff0-f962391fad28.name: Sanayeh Garden
f3942bb8-28a9-5994-bff0-f962391fad28.description: This green lung of the city is very popular among the neighbourhood residents. The garden features a large Ottoman fountain and covers a total surface area of 22,000 square metres.
f3942bb8-28a9-5994-bff0-f962391fad28.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
f3942bb8-28a9-5994-bff0-f962391fad28.history: The garden is one of the oldest public open-air spaces in the capital. Khalil Pasha (1864–1923), commander of the Turkish Sixth Army during World War I, had the park built in 1907. The park has had many names since its construction in the early 20th century, It was first called the Hamidi Public Garden, but was renamed the René Muawad Garden in honour of President René Muawad, who was assassinated nearby on November 22, 1989. However, it has been referred to as Sanayeh Park by the public for decades.
f3942bb8-28a9-5994-bff0-f962391fad28.keywords: Beirut; Sanayeh; Garden; Public; Space; René Muawad

f5f16dbd-27d3-5ffd-a0d0-e14c06b55466.name: *Terraces*
f5f16dbd-27d3-5ffd-a0d0-e14c06b55466.archival: Berbrugger, *Algérie Historique Pittoresque et Monumentale*, Paris: J. Delahaye, 1843.

f659e676-c7e7-5974-ace5-795fdd1ed49b.name: *Bayt Lisbuna, Damascus*
f659e676-c7e7-5974-ace5-795fdd1ed49b.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
f659e676-c7e7-5974-ace5-795fdd1ed49b.author: Stefan Weber
f659e676-c7e7-5974-ace5-795fdd1ed49b.second_name: Inhabitants in the courtyard demonstrating the new style of decoration and clothing
f659e676-c7e7-5974-ace5-795fdd1ed49b.description2: The Bayt Lisbuna saw two major construction phases. The existing structures date from the 19th century (around 1810) and were remodelled after 1865 and 1872. This house of a Jewish family like many other houses of Muslim or Christian families underwent major changes in style and plan at the end of the 19th and beginning of the 20th centuries. Several thousand private homes were adopted to the new modern style, with a radical change in techniques and forms of decoration. While still being a Damascene courtyard house these monuments of private taste became witness of a comprehensive urban change in the light of an entangled modernity.

f92e54e2-12d0-5aaf-9ae2-ccb42b9f2df7.name: The monuments in the Hippodrome surrounded by protective fences
f92e54e2-12d0-5aaf-9ae2-ccb42b9f2df7.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
f92e54e2-12d0-5aaf-9ae2-ccb42b9f2df7.description2: Robertson’s Istanbul photographs are concerned primarily with the city’s historical monuments. They reveal the city’s magnificent Byzantine and Ottoman structures from different angles and with close-ups taken in an approach that is usually quite aesthetic. A frequently employed device in Robertson's photographs is the inclusion of the one or more human figures in the foreground – indeed, this is something of a trademark of Robertson’s work. In this photo, the monuments in the Hippodrome are surrounded by protective fences.

fa5098a6-c21a-55a5-9278-ef4b943a399c.name: Arched house
fa5098a6-c21a-55a5-9278-ef4b943a399c.description: The internal layout varied from house to house: the distribution of rooms, the location of the gallery, the regularity of the plan, or the inclusion of a protruding/external central element. As the house is organised around a large central arc, the different wings open up onto a central arcade rather than directly communicating with each other. The arcade itself serves as a porch and a circulation space, facilitating transition and structuring life around the open air. During the colder months, however, a reception room indoors is used as the house's centrepiece.
fa5098a6-c21a-55a5-9278-ef4b943a399c.author: Jeff El-Msanne, David Andos
fa5098a6-c21a-55a5-9278-ef4b943a399c.history: The "arcade house" is a relatively old architectural style which was in vogue mostly before the 19th century. This style of house can be found in both rural and urban settings, and even within walled cities (?), as demonstrated by old photographs of Beirut. These houses were generally built with *ramleh* stone and a slanted roof. The house was designed on a principle of scalability, meaning it was able to grow in size without altering its internal logic.

fbf36d0e-1c98-5536-895f-1b9eff88b55c.name: *The Place du Gouvernement in Algiers*
fbf36d0e-1c98-5536-895f-1b9eff88b55c.author: Dalila Orfali
fbf36d0e-1c98-5536-895f-1b9eff88b55c.description2: Albert Marquet spent 1904 and 1907 in the company of Fauve, and in 1913 he lived in Tangier with Matisse and Camoin. Seven years later in 1920 he visited Algiers for the first time, and went on to spent a few months there every year henceforth. He also lived in Algiers for the duration of the Second World War. Marquet was friendly with most of the artists from the Algerian school, and exhibited his paintings in galleries in the centre of town. Many of his paintings were on the theme of Algiers' harbour. In 1939, his friends from the Salle Bordes organised his first solo exhibition. His style, which was characterised by the luminosity and clarity he saw in North Africa, was an important early influence on the Algerian painter Mohamed Temam.

fbf3f354-9bf0-5444-bf1c-c67f39eba7dc.name: Saint Louis Capuchin Church
fbf3f354-9bf0-5444-bf1c-c67f39eba7dc.description: Saint Louis Capuchin Cathedral is a Latin Catholic cathedral located in downtown Beirut, north of the Grand Serail. The church was built in 1864 by capuchin missionaries and is named after King Louis IX of France. It is recognisable by its sandstone facades, rose-coloured wooden windows, and the new towering bell tower.
fbf3f354-9bf0-5444-bf1c-c67f39eba7dc.author: Julien El Khoury, Jeff El-Msanne
fbf3f354-9bf0-5444-bf1c-c67f39eba7dc.history: When the capuchin missionaries first arrived in Lebanon in 1628 they worshipped at the old Saint George Church (where today's Maronite cathedral stands) in downtown Beirut. In 1732, they built the first church of their own near today's Riadh al-Solh square, dedicated to King Louis IX of France. In 1868 they relocated to Bab Idris and inaugurated the current cathedral. This cathedral was used for official celebrations during the French Mandate period. The church was raided in December 1975 and was a site of fierce fighting during the Lebanese civil war, during which time it was severely damaged by fire. The cathedral was the first landmark to be rebuilt in Downtown Beirut following the war, and was reopened in 2002.
fbf3f354-9bf0-5444-bf1c-c67f39eba7dc.keywords: Church; Crusader; Religion; Catholic; Mass; Beirut

fc5492b4-b79e-5ab6-acf3-8e4d44f66cbc.name: The villa of Paul Draneht in Oggebbio (Verbania, Italy)
fc5492b4-b79e-5ab6-acf3-8e4d44f66cbc.author: Massimiliano Cremona, Ignazio Galella
fc5492b4-b79e-5ab6-acf3-8e4d44f66cbc.archival: Intra: Tipografia Intrese, no date (but postal stamp of 1906)
fc5492b4-b79e-5ab6-acf3-8e4d44f66cbc.description2:
In 1872, Paul Draneht Bey bought a Villa on the Lago Maggiore (Italy), which he remodelled, mixing oriental and European architectural styles. From this postcard, one can see a tower with an Arabic flavour.  
In the interior, there was an “Egyptian hall”, modelled according to the style of an ancient Upper-Egypt temple. The furniture was made by one of the shops in Paris that was making the scenes for the opera *Aida*.

fcc8f922-ec2a-5d70-8123-eab8d9f5b00c.name: Photo showing the Institute of Medicine
fcc8f922-ec2a-5d70-8123-eab8d9f5b00c.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
fcc8f922-ec2a-5d70-8123-eab8d9f5b00c.keywords: Faculty; Medicine; Pharmacy; USJ; SJU; University; Education
fcc8f922-ec2a-5d70-8123-eab8d9f5b00c.description2: The Medical school at the Université Saint Joseph (USJ) was established by the French state in 1883. The French state provided funding, a curriculum, and professors. Later that same year, following an agreement between the Jesuits and the French government, the Institute of Medicine opened on the university's campus. This was later followed by the opening of many other institutes, such as the faculties of law, economics and management, and literature. On 6 October 1888, the French government recognized the institute as part of a Faculty of Medicine. In 1889, when the school of pharmacy was founded, it was renamed as the Faculty of Medicine and Pharmacy.

fcea3c25-ab06-5b64-9498-f2354cb75232.name: Ortaköy Mosque
fcea3c25-ab06-5b64-9498-f2354cb75232.description2: The change of perception towards the role of the sultan brought about the construction of the Imperial kiosk '*hünkar kasrı*' in front of the mosques built by sultans.

ff3e8256-d8ee-5d47-b909-e92dca381df5.name: Ortaköy Mosque
ff3e8256-d8ee-5d47-b909-e92dca381df5.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
ff3e8256-d8ee-5d47-b909-e92dca381df5.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; Mosques; Ancient Istanbul
ff3e8256-d8ee-5d47-b909-e92dca381df5.description2: The Ortaköy Mosque was ordered by the Ottoman sultan Abdülmecid and built between 1854 and 1856. Its architects were father and son Garabet Amira Balyan and Nigoğayos Balyan (who also designed the nearby Dolmabahçe Palace and the Dolmabahçe Mosque), who designed it in the Neo-Baroque style.

ff78af46-329b-5d7b-810a-cacb6d484374.name: Umm al-Rasas
ff78af46-329b-5d7b-810a-cacb6d484374.dates: Roman-Present; identified in 1896 by J. Germer-Durand
ff78af46-329b-5d7b-810a-cacb6d484374.author: Mohammad Najjar
ff78af46-329b-5d7b-810a-cacb6d484374.history: The World Heritage Site of Umm al-Rasas (Kastron Mefa'a, Kastrom Mefa'a) is an archaeological site in Jordan which contains ruins from the Roman, Byzantine, and early Muslim periods. The most important monument in the site was the mosaic floor of the Church of St Stephen. This biggest mosaic floor in Jordan – which was built in 785 AD – depicts the most important cities in Jordan, Palestine and Egypt. The fact that the mosaic floor was constructed during the Abbasid period reflects the spirit of tolerance and co-existence of the Muslim and Christian communities during that period. Umm al-Rasas was visited by H.B. Tristram in 1872 and subsequently identified in 1896 by J. Germer-Durand with the Biblical and Late Antiquity city of Mephaath.
ff78af46-329b-5d7b-810a-cacb6d484374.keywords: World Heritage Site; frontier station; Archaeological investigations; churches; mosaic panels; Tristram
ff78af46-329b-5d7b-810a-cacb6d484374.description2: The town of Umm al-Rasas was enclosed in an almost square (app.160x155 meters) enclosure surrounded by fortification walls and 24 towers. The main gateway was from the east. Two small gates were positioned at the north and the south sides. These were blocked later. Archaeological investigations at the site were concentrated on the four churches identified inside the fortification walls, including the church of the Rivers and the church of the Palm tree. These were named after the main component of the mosaic panels on the floors. At least 11 other churches were identified outside the enclosure to the north. The most prominent of them are the church of St. Stephen with its famous mosaic panels of 15 major towns of Jordan and Palestine of the time.

ffecc84b-856d-5f87-97de-682a1d90e53d.name: *View of Istanbul: the Valide Sultan Mosque and the port*
ffecc84b-856d-5f87-97de-682a1d90e53d.second_name: Taken from the collection *Photographies Positives* by Pascal Sébah
ffecc84b-856d-5f87-97de-682a1d90e53d.description2: Pascal Sébah (1823–1886) was a French photographer working in the Ottoman capital Constantinople, where he developed a successful trade selling photographs to European tourists and lovers of Orientalism. The great changes Constantinople underwent towards the end of the 19th century are evident in this image. The Valide Sutlan Mosque dominates the Eminönü port, which had become very prosperous during the Ottoman era thanks to active trading with the West. The construction of the Galata bridge, the Orient Express railway line, and the arrival of steam-boats also contributed to its development.
